picks.headline: Staff predictions for Virginia Tech-SMU: Can the Hokies triumph in Dallas?
picks.blurb: Virginia Tech football takes on SMU in Dallas, Texas, today, striving to improve to 7-2 (4-2 ACC) in its first year under head coach James Franklin. Ahead of the clash, here's our staff's predictions as to what will unfold tonight in the Lone Star State. JACKSON CAUDELL: While it will still be a long shot even if they find a way to win, the Hokies' ACC hopes are on the line tomorrow night at SMU. The Mustangs are also battling for their ACC title hopes, and that makes this a fascinating matchup. This is a chance for James Franklin to land another win against one of the better programs in the conference, and I think they have the offense to take advantage of a suspect SMU defense. If the Hokies can get after Kevin Jennings and force a few turnovers, I think they are able to do that and score a big win. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 31, SMU 27 JAMES DUNCAN: Syracuse left a blueprint last Saturday, beating SMU 30-27 on a touchdown with 17 seconds left. Virginia Tech is built to follow it. Nobody has beaten the Hokies by more than five points this season, and they come in with 13 days of rest to SMU’s six. Ethan Grunkemeyer has thrown 17 touchdowns and two interceptions, and both picks came in one night against Pitt. He won’t hand Kevin Jennings free possessions, which puts the game on Brent Pry’s defense. That group made 13 tackles for loss at Clemson, and it won’t need half that many Friday if it gets off the field on third down. Friday won’t be a rout, but I think the Hokies give the Mustangs their first home loss in the ACC. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 30, SMU 28 THOMAS HUGHES: Let's get this out of the way: SMU has never lost an ACC game at home. Its strongest wins at Gerald J. Ford Stadium this season, however, came against Virginia and California — two squads with a combined 7-11 (4-8 ACC) record. The Hokies should be well-equipped to contend with the Mustangs, though SMU signal-caller Kevin Jennings may present Tech with its toughest test of the season yet. Virginia Tech quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer has been stellar this campaign, throwing 17 touchdowns to just two interceptions, and while I expect another strong performance from him, I think SMU narrowly edges Virginia Tech in Dallas tonight. Final score prediction: SMU 31, Virginia Tech 28 KADEN REINHARD: I think this game will be defined by one word over the 60 minutes of action: Intensity. Several factors will fuel that fire: Friday night lights, the Mustangs coming off the Syracuse loss and Tech finding itself back in the receiving-votes category of the AP Top 25. But most importantly, I see both offenses locking into a close-knit battle, as both sides can mend their attacks with a healthy mix of the ground and air attack. Ultimately, I think the Hokies' defense can handle the contest by not allowing SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings to extend many plays outside the pocket, which has been a struggle for the Hokies in recent years. At the same time, Ethan Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech's aerial attack provide a viable path to the full-game Over, regardless of whether SMU secures the victory. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p. m. TOP PICK Who will win Virginia Tech vs SMU: SMU -5.5 Play the SMU Mustangs to cover -5.5 at 54% or less. SMU has a more reliable path to multiple touchdown drives than the Virginia Tech Hokies . The Mustangs succeed on 50.4% of offensive snaps, ninth nationally , and QB Kevin Jennings generates 0.31 EPA per dropback. Virginia Tech's fifth-ranked havoc rate can wreck a possession, but it still allows successful plays on 43.4% of snaps . The Hokies can't count on a sack or takeaway to end every drive, and with Jennings' ability to avoid sacks, the task for a havoc-reliant team becomes much more difficult. At the other end, Virginia Tech's ground game produces a near-negative EPA per rush, inviting SMU to put Ethan Grunkemeyer in obvious passing situations. The bye helps the Hokies' preparation, but keeping this within five requires them to disrupt Jennings repeatedly while sustaining enough drives of their own. I expect SMU's offensive edge to produce a full-touchdown margin. Virginia Tech vs SMU Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 Play the Over 55.5 at 53% or less. SMU's defense allows 4.58 points per opponent scoring opportunity, 112th nationally . That gives Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech a route to points even if they can't control the game. The Hokies have thrown effectively enough to threaten downfield, while SMU's defense has been better at preventing long drives than finishing stops once opponents cross the 40. On the other side, the Mustangs produce explosive plays on 9.9% of snaps, eighth nationally . Their scoring doesn't have to consume much clock. I expect SMU to set the pace and Virginia Tech to contribute enough through the air to clear this full-game number. Jennings can punish a defense that gets aggressive without ending the possession and he's hard to do that against. Tech also allows a successful play on 44.6% of opposing dropbacks, giving the Mustangs chances to throw through pressure rather than repeatedly challenge its front. Kendrick Raphael's eight rushing touchdowns give SMU a dependable option near the goal line. Virginia Tech vs SMU combo I like this combo because Virginia Tech should be healthier up front. James Franklin said the bye should bring offensive linemen Montavious Cunningham and Brody Meadows back. picks.blurb: Virginia Tech Hokies vs. SMU Mustangs: News, Information, and Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Virginia Tech Hokies vs. SMU Mustangs: News, Information, and Predictions Stike up the Hokie Pokey, Tech Triumph, and the Victory Tag. | John Schneider - SB Nation John Schneider · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:59 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's a short week after a week break. The Hokies are heading to Dallas to face off against the Southern Methodist University Mustangs. The Hokies are up against another major ACC opponent, and winning the game means advancing in the ACC and potentially seeing a ranking. Crossover Week Mayhem Just a note from us: Well, the first week in November through the first week of December is always a challenge for coverage. The soccer teams are wrapping up with decent enough records, but their seasons aren't quite over. The Women's Basketball Team has opened their home record at 2-0, and the Men's team also graced Cassell with a W. All of that puts a real strain on coverage so bear with us as we sort out schedules, and fight fall health issues and work vs. Hokie sports balance. The football team isn't finished, though. There are still four games left on the schedule, and then we get to plan on bowl coverage this season. Isn't that a happy event? The Hokies are bowl eligible just a couple of games after the halfway point, and that's a very pleasant occurrence. To think that we are actually paying attention to the bowl invitation list, instead of worrying on Thanksgiving weekend whether or not a win will net an invitation somewhere. The first thing to cover is a bit of fun. The ACC Network desk hosts Eric McClain and Eddie Royal had a bet going. Remember, McClain is a former Clemson player, and we all know and love Eddie Royal. So, the bet was that the loser had to wear the winner's mascot costume. Eddie was not dressed as a Tiger with the googly eyes for the TV segment. ( Congratulations to the Virginia Tech Cheer Squad equipment folks and Travis Wells for getting most of an actual Hokie Bird big enough for Eric. ) The Virginia Tech Wrestling Team received a massive boost from a wrestler who hasn't even wrestled his first match as a Hokie, yet, but who is already a world champion. Freshman Bo Bassett traveled to Kazakhstan and netted the program its first world championship and was the first American in 20 years to win in his weight class (65KG – for those lacking metric conversion skills that's 143 pounds ). The Coach Robie is going to have an absolutely dominant wrestling team this season. Back to Football Stuff It looks like the team is going to be wearing head to toe all-whites for this one. Go get your coffee, or a quick snack and listen in on Coach Franklin's weekly presser. As Bryan posted up earlier, this time the Hokies have some really good news coming out of the locker room as it pertains to the Offensive Line. Montavious Cunningham and Brody Meadows are back up to speed and are expected to play on Friday night. The O-Line has been dipping into the #3s on the depth chart for the past few games, and getting them back is a serious update to the struggling run game. That All Leads to This… Predictions The SMU Mustangs are largely a Big XII import with a near automatic bubble to the top of the ACC football pile. It's Dallas, TX, and football is a near religion for Texas. That means the program is well funded, with premium coaching, and players doused liberally with NIL funding. Up until last weekend, the Mustangs were sporting a very respectable one loss record. Until they showed up in the Syracuse (whatever they call the Carrier Dome, now), as expected in the beginning of the season SMU was challenging hard for the #2 bid in the ACC fake Championship game ( until the conference goes back to divisions and division champs who play everyone else in the division the game in Charlotte will remain fake to me ). Then the Mustangs got treated to the old Big East upset win by the Orange. That knocked them down a peg but also put the Hokies in the position of earning the #3 spot on the ACC leader board. That all means that this game might not mean an ACC bid, but it will mean a much better bowl game situation over the holidays. Bowls mean big broadcast money, and the program needs the cash to make up for a restricted gate at Lane. The Mustangs are favored by slightly less than a touchdown for this one, in their house no less. We'll see how we feel about that. This is a big test for the Hokies. Virginia Tech had a huge win at Clemson two weeks ago. No, this isn't the same Clemson team as only a few years ago, but it means something for other ACC teams to walk into Death Valley and win. SMU is better than the Tigers, but they aren't unbeatable. The clear difference here is the quarterback position. SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings is a stud. He also has one of the ACC's best running backs and one of the top receiving units in the league. This is a huge challenge for VT defensive coordinator Brent Pry. Offensively, I think the Hokies have success moving the ball. SMU's size on the defensive interior concerns me, especially with Tech's OL struggles. There is hope that with Cunningham and Meadows back, the offensive line is better, but we'll see. I expect a close game. My heart says the Hokies, my head says SMU in a close one. SMU 34, Hokies 31 This game all depends on how the Mustangs adjusted to their Syracuse loss, and if the Hokies on both sides of the ball can adjust to how the Orange controlled the SMU offense, and how they managed to get by their defense. SMU, interestingly enough, has a similar offensive/defensive balance to Tech's than we have seen this season. There are lots of "IFs" in this game, and the biggest one is "IF" the Tech defense can limit the SMU offense to what it's been scoring over the season against peer teams, the Hokies have a much better chance to win than the listed 6-point betting gimme to SMU. The latest projected O/U is 56.5, which tells me volumes of information. The analysts see this as a very close game, and the end result being less than a full score between the two teams. If the Hokies stay away from getting enamored of the run game and go downfield fast and consistently in the air on quick developing intermediate routes to their best receivers, there will be run opportunities. If Tech decides to try to "establish the run" the offense could bog down into chronic 3-and-outs. The return of two key #1/#2 depth chart players is not an excuse to try to revert to 1960's caveman Johnny Unitas two runs and a pass offense. If the Hokies move the ball and do it fast, they have enough defense ( which needs to put serious pressure on the quarterback on every play ) to hold the Mustangs to a 3.5 score effort. The Hokies are capable of 4 or more. That's a whole lot of "Ifs" though. Here's the skinny… the first team to score over 30 points wins. That puts my prediction hat on, and I think the Hokies might just be good for it, regardless of the conditions. Just a quick reminder of the times and broadcast information. It's an ESPN deal.

picks.blurb: Virginia Tech vs SMU Prediction: Setting Up the Showdowns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Virginia Tech vs SMU Prediction: Setting Up the Showdowns Pete Fiutak · College Football News Wed, November 4, 2026 at 9:28 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There's still a chance for both SMU and Virginia Tech to get into the ACC Championship, but can either one step up and take control of the opportunity? SMU had everything there for the taking. It gets Wake Forest in Dallas next week, closes the ACC season at Stanford, but everything got upended in a loss to Syracuse 30-27. Win out, though, and it has a great shot when it comes down to the tiebreakers. Virginia Tech has won two in a row, and it gets Miami in a few weeks. If it wins out, including a win over the Canes, it'll be in a great position to slip into the College Football Playoff. Virginia Tech vs SMU: Quick Hits SMU (6-2) hosts Wake Forest next before the massive moment at Notre Dame. Virginia Tech (6-2) gets Stanford next before going to Miami and closing with the rivalry date against Virginia. The two haven't played since an SMU 28-25 win in 1974. The Mustangs went 2-1 from 1972 to 1974 . How To Watch Virginia Tech vs SMU Date: Friday, November 6, 2026 Game Time: 7:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium, Dallas, TX – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Virginia Tech Will Win The Hokies defensive line continues to seek and destroy opposing offenses. Virginia Tech is No. 1 in the nation in tackles for loss, coming up with 13 in the win over Clemson two weeks ago, along with four sacks. SMU is okay in pass protection, and it's solid at times with the running game, but there's a problem when it turns the ball over – the two giveaways against Syracuse were a big deal. The three turnovers in the loss to Louisville mattered. However … Why SMU Will Win Virginia Tech doesn't take the ball away enough. The two takeaways helped stop Georgia Tech in a 34-24 win, but the Hokies have only forced six turnovers, and none in five games. SMU has to get its tempo going. Counteract the Virginia Tech pass rush with quick-hitting throws, keep the defense on its heels, and, on the other side, get the defense off the field. Virginia Tech isn't always great on third downs, and SMU is third in the nation, with offenses converting just 27% of their chances. Virginia Tech vs SMU Prediction, Betting Lines SMU is a much different team in Gerald J. Ford. The offense is good no matter where it plays, but this year, the defense steps its game up several notches, especially against the run. The three worst games on the season for the run defense were all on the road, and the Hokies won't grind it out enough. Virginia Tech is 2-2 when it doesn't get to 130 yards on the ground. SMU hasn't allowed more than 125 this year at home. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Virginia Tech vs. SMU
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Virginia Tech vs. SMU - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Three Bold Predictions for Virginia Tech vs. SMU Virginia Tech Hokies tight end Luke Reynolds (85) scores near Clemson safety Jerome Carter III (6) during the second quarter at Memorial Stadium Saturday, October 24, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect James Duncan · Virginia Tech Hokies On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:37 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Seventeen seconds remained in the JMA Wireless Dome on Saturday, when Syracuse quarterback Steve Angeli found tight end Noah Meyers alone on the left side of the end zone. Meyers had never scored for the Orange before that catch. The touchdown beat SMU 30-27 and knocked the Mustangs out of the AP Top 25. Virginia Tech should have that clip on a loop. The Hokies (6-2, 3-2 ACC) visit SMU (6-2, 4-2) at 7 p.m. ET Friday on ESPN. The Mustangs are 5-0 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium this season and 6.5-point favorites. Their defense holds up better against the pass than the run, and its injuries are stacked in the middle of the field. Two of my predictions start there. The third starts with what Syracuse did to Kevin Jennings. 1. Luke Reynolds has his best game since September SMU doesn't give much away through the air. Opponents complete 62.6% of their passes and average 6.0 yards per attempt. The one real hole is at safety. Sophomore Tyren Polley Jr., third on the team with 34 tackles, tore a pectoral muscle in October and is out for the season. SMU has played two games without him: a 59-20 win over Cal and the loss at Syracuse. Help could be coming. Ahmaad Moses, a first-team All-ACC safety in 2025, is questionable after missing the whole season while SMU works on his eligibility. The junior tight end has 50 catches for 493 yards and six touchdowns, and his 50 catches lead all FBS tight ends. The last three games have been quieter: 13 catches for 120 yards since Pitt. Two of those 13 went for touchdowns at Clemson, including the go-ahead score in the fourth quarter. Friday, he clears 100 receiving yards for the third time this season and finds the end zone again. 2. Jeffrey Overton Jr. snaps his 100-yard drought Overton last reached 100 yards on Sept. 26, when he ran for 209 at Boston College, the sixth-highest single-game total in Virginia Tech history. He has 230 yards in four games since and averaged 2.6 yards per carry at Clemson. The sophomore still leads the Hokies with 639 yards on 113 carries. Two things change Friday. The first is the offensive line. "We're going to get some guys back, which is helpful, especially on the offensive line," coach James Franklin said Monday. Guard/tackle Montavious Cunningham and guard Brody Meadows are expected to play. Left tackle Justin Terry is still out. The second is the defense across from him. SMU allows 125.9 rushing yards per game and 3.8 yards per carry. Those numbers flatter the Mustangs. College football counts sacks as rushing plays, and SMU has 23 sacks for 148 yards. Pull them out, and opponents are averaging 4.8 yards per designed run. Those 23 sacks matter for Virginia Tech in another way. Ethan Grunkemeyer has been sacked 23 times himself. A run game that works keeps the Hokies on schedule and gives SMU's rushers something else to think about. Overton gets his third 100-yard game of the season. 3. Virginia Tech sacks Kevin Jennings at least four times Before Halloween, SMU hadn't allowed more than two sacks in a game this season. Syracuse got six. Look at who was playing on the left side. True freshman Drew Evers moved over from right tackle to start at left tackle, and fellow true freshman Sam Utu made his first career start beside him at left guard. It was only the second college game of his career. SMU could get some help back. Guard Alex Woods, a starter, missed Syracuse, and tackle Andrew Chamblee, who has started at both tackle spots, hasn't played since Oct. 17. Neither is on Thursday's availability report. Watch the first series to see who lines up on the left. Either way, Virginia Tech has the rushers to test it. The Hokies average 3.4 sacks per game, sixth in FBS, and three players have more than four: Aycen Stevens with eight, Cortez Harris with five and Mylachi Williams with 4.5. Defensive tackle Kemari Copeland said this week the plan is to "cage" Jennings and take away his scrambles to the right. Friday, the Hokies get to Jennings at least four times. Tunmise Adeleye's 6-yard sack of Kevin Jennings helped force a three-and-out that gave the Orange their opportunity. Syracuse has the ball at its own 32-yard line with 3:35 remaining in the fourth quarter, trailing No. 19 SMU 27-23 after forcing a three-and-out. Angeli's return gives Syracuse momentum It was Angeli's fifth game with multiple touchdown passes in eight Syracuse starts. His return followed a stretch in which the Orange used five quarterbacks, including two other starters. Syracuse quarterback Amari Odom out for season following shoulder surgery, Malachi Nelson sidelined several weeks Watch & listen ▾ Our shows Syracuse rallied for a 30-27 win over SMU with a late touchdown drive. Chase Geter recovered a fumble on the Mustangs' final possession to preserve the victory. Syracuse rallies past No. 19 SMU, 30-27 Syracuse rallied with a late touchdown drive and recovered a fumble on SMU's final possession to beat the No. 19 Mustangs 30-27 Saturday at the JMA Wireless Dome. Steve Angeli found Noah Meyers for a 2-yard, go-ahead touchdown with 17 seconds remaining, and Tripp Woody added the extra point to finish an 11-play, 68-yard drive that took 3:19, according to Syracuse's official statistics and the ACC Digital Network highlight . The Orange improved to 4-4 overall and 2-4 in the ACC, while SMU fell to 6-2 and 4-2 in conference play. Late scoring drive completes the comeback After Syracuse moved ahead, Braheem Long Jr. broke up a deep pass intended for Jalen Cooper. On the final play, Randy Pittman Jr. attempted a lateral after catching a pass from Jennings. Geter recovered the loose ball, returned it 13 yards and went down to end the game, according to Syracuse's expanded official recap . Steve Angeli completed 21 of 34 passes for 200 yards and a touchdown. Umari Hatcher had six catches for 65 yards, Daunte Bacheyie had three for 47 and Calvin Russell III caught three for 41. Clement keeps the winning drive alive Angeli opened the final scoring drive with completions of 7 yards to Bacheyie and 13 to Hatcher, then found Darius Johnson for 6 yards. After Ju'Juan Johnson gained 3 yards, David Clement caught a 7-yard pass on fourth-and-1 to keep the possession alive. Russell and Bacheyie followed with 15-yard receptions, with Bacheyie reaching the SMU 2. After a run for no gain, Syracuse called timeout with 19 seconds left. Angeli then found Meyers on the left side for the winning touchdown. Orange answer after SMU scores 17 straight Syracuse led 20-10 at halftime before SMU scored 17 unanswered points. Kendrick Raphael's 13-yard touchdown run with 9:04 left in the fourth quarter helped put the Mustangs ahead 27-20. No. 7 BYU visits No. 3 Utah on Saturday, November 7, in the first Holy War where both teams are ranked in the top 10. The 10 a.m. local kickoff at Rice-Eccles Stadium adds another wrinkle. Utah is 8–0 and sits atop the Big 12 at 5–0. BYU is 7–1 and shares second place with Texas Tech, but its loss to UCF leaves little room for error. Utah opened as roughly a 5.5-point favorite with a total of 48.5. These predictions go against the safe script, a ground-game surprise, a Utah quarterback performance and a late BYU rally that falls short. Let's take a look at the bold predictions for this marquee matchup. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) LJ Martin plays, but Bear Bachmeier is the star Rob Gray-Imagn Images LJ Martin will return and play a limited role, yet Bachmeier will be the one who carries BYU's offense. Martin has missed four games with a leg injury and has not played since the October 3 win over TCU. He is still BYU's leading rusher at 344 yards and 7.8 yards per carry, so the Cougars badly need him. But offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick said Martin is "not all the way back yet," which suggests a managed workload. The prediction is Bachmeier throws for 275 yards and rushes for two touchdowns, outproducing Martin in every category. Bachmeier has already accounted for most of BYU's rushing output without Martin, with 336 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns on 80 carries. He also has 1,750 passing yards and 12 touchdowns. Utah's secondary is among the best in the country, so BYU may need Martin's presence as a decoy more than as a workhorse. That could open play-action and RPO looks for Bachmeier. Devon Dampier and Wayshawn Parker combine for 300 total yards Utah's offense will hinge on its quarterback and running back, and together they will account for 300 total yards and four touchdowns. Dampier has been outstanding, with 12 total touchdowns against one interception over his last four games. He has completed 69.6 percent of his passes for 1,876 yards and 18 touchdowns this season. Parker is the other half. He has 726 rushing yards and nine touchdowns, and Utah's ground game ranks eighth nationally at 226.9 yards per game. BYU's rush defense is strong in raw yardage, ranking 20th at 100 yards per game, but Covers notes it ranks only 74th in rush success rate. That gap suggests Utah can win with misdirection and efficiency instead of pure power. The Utes also rank third nationally in third-down efficiency at 54.1 percent, which helps them sustain drives against an aggressive linebacker group. Utah will lose right tackle Kelvin Obot for the season, but the line has still been one of the best in the country. I expect the Utes to handle his absence. Utah wins 31–27 and snaps BYU's three-game streak The final prediction is a four-point Utah win that comes down to the last possession. BYU has won three straight in the series, while Utah had won nine in a row before that. Utah has still won 14 straight overall, the longest active streak in the FBS. Utah's offense should control the game early, but BYU will keep it close by converting in the red zone. A late Cougars touchdown will make it a one-possession game before the Utes' defense finishes with a stop. The projected 58 total points would clear the 48.5-point line comfortably. The point spread would also come down to a single score, giving BYU a cover as a 5.5-point underdog. The result would leave Utah in prime position for a Big 12 title game berth and a playoff bid. BYU would stay alive in the conference race, but it would have almost no margin left. No. 9 BYU @ No. 3 Utah This Holy War might be the holiest of them all: Utah hosting bitter rival BYU, with the winner in the driver's seat for a Playoff spot. It’s the first time both teams have been ranked in the top 10 for this matchup, and I can’t wait to start the day with this one. I think BYU might win outright. It has been tested with its win over Notre Dame just a few weeks ago. Yes, it lost to UCF the following week in a typical trap game — big home win followed by a road conference game. Otherwise, the Cougars have handled business, even though the scores don’t seem that impressive. BYU is built on defense. It is 13th in yards per play and it limits explosives. It does not rush the passer all that well, but against Utah’s rushing attack, that might not be needed. BYU’s defense already faced a high-powered offense in the Irish and limited it to a negative EPA rushing day. Utah’s offensive production slowly ticked down when conference play started, but it did bounce back last week against a poor Cincinnati defense. Utah has played one defense in the same realm as BYU and that was Houston. Utah struggled to score, only putting up 21 points with seven of those happening super late after forcing a Houston turnover. Will the BYU offense find a groove against Utah? (Getty Images) It’s fair to also believe BYU’s offense might struggle in this game. However, it appears the Cougars are getting stud running back LJ Martin back, and they are much better when Martin is on the field. He’s averaging almost eight yards a carry with 20% of his rushes going for 10+ yards. Utah’s defense is the typical physical front against the run, but BYU is the best offense the Utes have faced all season. Utah’s pass rush concerns me. It is 80th in pressure rate and unless it blitzes, it isn't able to get to the quarterback. Seems less than ideal against BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier. I see these teams as even. They are both defensively based with an offense that wants to run the ball. That’s too many points in a game like this. I’ll take BYU to cover. Quarterback Keelon Russell is nearing the end of his first season as a starting quarterback, and he’s been mostly excellent for his age. However, he has struggled the last three weeks outside the end of the Texas A&M game. Against Georgia, Tennessee and A&M, he completed only 60% of passes with just four passing touchdowns and three interceptions. Alabama’s beat-up offensive line has allowed 11 sacks in the three previous games. Now, the Tide play an LSU defense that’s first in sacks per pressure and 11th in pressure rate. The Bama offensive line and Russell were noticeably affected by the environment in Tennessee, and now they are at LSU. I feel most comfortable with Alabama not scoring much in this game. They're backed into a corner. So, don't we all expect to get Notre Dame's best? I mean, we have to … Now, Miami has taken care of business. Notre Dame did not. They got beat by BYU. What's the weakest thing that any of these teams do? Well, if you're looking at the weakest thing, I always look at that, because in a matchup game typically the weakest link of the teams is what's going to end up getting you beat, and the weakest thing that anybody does in this game is Miami's defense, and we've seen that over the last, what, three weeks and three games. Two of the last three games, they've given up 35 points to Florida State and UNC. So it's not a great defense. It is not nearly the defensive front that they had a year ago. Their secondary is not great. "So they've got to find a way to limit CJ Carr, who I think is one of the better quarterbacks that we have in the country. What's the strongest part of this game? It's Miami's offense. It's interesting. They've got the strongest part. They've got the weakest part. Their ceiling with their offense is outstanding. I think it's the best thing anybody does in college football. Darian Mensah film is fantastic. I love watching it. "I'm going to go to Notre Dame. I think that they have to win, and they will win because, again, the committee is doing Miami no favors here … Notre Dame 30-27. Miami, I'll take the 5.5." Klatt's straight-up pick: Notre Dame Klatt's pick against the spread: Miami +5.5 No. 9 BYU vs. No. 3 Utah (Photo by Bryan Byerly/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) Spread: Utah -4.5 Moneyline: Utah -198, BYU +164 Klatt's thoughts: "BYU at Utah. Holy War. 4.5 is the spread here. Utah is favored. Utah has lost three straight in this series, including a home game. BYU has not looked great since the Notre Dame game. I think we would all agree with that. Utah has been a team that has been very impressive, which is largely why they're ranked No. 3 in the country right now. Because even though they've played something north of a wet paper bag, the committee decided that they were the third-ranked team in the country. That was a shot. It wasn't meant to be a shot. Because I love Utah. You know I love you, Utah. Death, taxes, Utah football. They roared back against Houston after being down 10-0 at around halftime. They destroyed Cincinnati. They're a difficult team to beat on the road when they're in their home stadium. Devon Dampier and Wayshawn Parker are dynamic. The one concern I would have for Devon Dampier is the turnovers. "You can't do that in this game, not in this game. And, in particular, with an aggressive BYU defense … They're going to have to run the football, play quality defense, and use the energy of that stadium to their benefit. LJ Martin for BYU could be back. I don't know how effective he will be, but they need that because they have not been able to run the football very well over the last couple of weeks. Speaking of BYU, both have good defenses. Although, gosh, you know I love Kalani Sitake. I think Kalani Sitake is fantastic, but his defense the last couple of weeks hasn't been like BYU standard. I personally believe this Utah team has something to prove. Almost like their coach retired and then took another job somewhere else. It's like it resembles that. I don't know if that was the case or not, but that's what it looks like. And Morgan Scalley has been there for a long time, and he understands the culture of Utah. And I think this team is playing with an edge. " Utah 27, BYU 20. Utah covers the 4.5." Klatt's straight-up pick: Utah Klatt's pick against the spread: Utah -4.5 No. 2 Georgia vs. No. 10 Ole Miss (Photo by Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) Spread: Georgia -3.5 Moneyline: Georgia -175, Ole Miss +145 Klatt's thoughts: "Georgia at Ole Miss. This one could be a great game. I really think it could be. Georgia is favored by 3.5. Rematch to that quarterfinal from a year ago. Ole Miss won that one. Trinidad Chambliss was outstanding in that ball game, and I'm sure Kirby Smart has had nightmares about Trinidad Chambliss ever since then. And now he's got to go to Oxford, and he's got to play Trinidad Chambliss where Trinidad Chambliss has never lost a start. Ole Miss is not going to have Kewan Lacy, he's likely out in this game. Trinidad Chambliss is a guy that I love. You guys, I know I've loved him ever since the beginning of the year, and now he gets to face Kirby Smart. And this team is the best road team that we have in the country over the last several years. Why? Because they're consistent. Why? Because they run the football. Because they play good defense. These are the things that travel. These are the things that allow you to have success on the road. I do think it's going to be a close game. I don't think Georgia is going to be able to separate in this game, but they're too consistent. They're too consistent. "If Georgia can hold Ole Miss to field goals, I think that's where the game is won or lost. If it's high scoring, I favor Ole Miss because Trinidad runs wild. If it's lower scoring and in the 20s, then I favor Georgia because it's a slug fest, and you're kicking field goals, and it's third down and it's situations. What do I think it's going to be? More of a slug fest. "I'm going to take Georgia 28-24 . They cover the 3.5 on the road." "This is not the same Ohio State that came into Eugene a couple of years ago and would eventually win the national championship. He overthrew some open wide receivers, and they didn't get the ball to Jeremiah Smith. "Jay Johnson is [Oregon's] new offensive coordinator after they fired Drew Mehringer after that Illinois game, and they looked a lot better in the second half against Northwestern. This is a very different defense than they're going to face. I think this is a much better secondary, and I would think that Matt Patricia of Ohio State is going to find a way to put pressure on Dylan Raiola. He does not deal with pressure well. It's like Ohio State's backed into a corner … You just get all of Ohio State, and if you get all of Ohio State, that means that you get all of Jeremiah Smith , and they're going to be taking shots, and they're going to be more aggressive even with a young quarterback, because you got nothing to lose. And when that happens, they have to protect their quarterback. And if they can't protect their quarterback, they don't win. And LSU is a terrific pass rushing team. Terrific, second in the country in sacks. Meanwhile, you would think that Alabama on the offensive line would do a good job protecting their quarterback. Not the case. We saw pressure against Tennessee, pressure against Georgia, and LSU might be better in the pass rush than both of those teams. Bad matchup. away.blurb: BYU Star LJ Martin Moving Closer to Return For Utah Game The No. 9 BYU Cougars are set to return Big 12 standout running back LJ Martin on Saturday against No. 3 Utah , according to multiple sources reporting that the senior is slated to dress. Martin moved up from “doubtful” to “questionable” on BYU's latest injury report for Week 10 at Utah, and, according to a Friday report by Pete Thamel at ESPN, Martin's spent the last three days actively participating in practice in hopes of seeing the field for Saturday's pivotal matchup that could shape the final three weeks of Big 12 football. Star tailback LJ Martin practiced the last three days for BYU. He’s on track to dress and attempt to play on Saturday. He’ll likely be limited, but he’s determined to impact the game. How he feels pre-game will determine extent of his role. https://t.co/Jaw1OsFKM3 Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today The Thamel report included that Martin is “determined to impact the game” on Saturday as the Cougars enter the matchup as a slight 4.5-point underdog . Martin's missed four consecutive weeks of football since enduring a lower-body injury during a 17-10 road win at TCU in early October. He's carried the ball 44 times for 344 yards, 3 touchdowns and an average of 7.8 yards per touch. Last year vs. then-No. 23 Utah, Martin rushed for 122 yards, 1 touchdown. BYU won the contest 24-21 in Provo, going on to finish the season 12-2 overall following a loss to Texas Tech in the Big 12 Championship Game at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. It'll be the first time the Cougars (7-1, 4-1 Big 12) and the Utes (8-0, 5-0), in the 98-year history of the football series, have been featured in the top 10. away.headline: BYU releases initial LJ Martin injury status ahead of Utah game
away.blurb: On Wednesday night, the BYU football program provided the first official injury update for LJ Martin ahead of a top 10 matchup with Utah. Martin is "doubtful" for the game against the Utes. The "doubtful" designation is reserved for the players that have a 25% chance to play. However, just a few minutes before the injury report came out, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Martin is considered "questionable" for this weekend. The "questionable" designation is reserved for players with a 50% chance to play. Thamel reported that if Martin returns, "he's not expected to be 100% and could be limited." Thamel added more information, saying "[Martin is] trending to dress, be available, and have some impact on the game. A final decision will be made later this week." Martin was back practicing on Tuesday, according to Aaron Roderick. The last time he played was in early October against TCU. If Martin can't go, BYU will turn to Preston Rex who was not available for the ASU game. Rex had a breakout game against Notre Dame before suffering an injury against UCF. If Saleapaga isn't available, expect more sets with three wide receivers. That would leave Walker Lyons on the field for most of the game. If Evan Johnson can't play, BYU will turn to Jayven Williams and Therrian Alexander III at cornerback. Williams and Alexander shut down two of the best wide receivers in the Big 12 last week. They are more than capable of holding it down on the outside. The bigger question will be who BYU plays at nickel. The Cougars started Cannon DeVries at that spot to start the season, but DeVries has primarily been used for punt return duties since he suffered an injury. The ASU game was the first time DeVries had seen defensive snaps since suffering the injury. He played 14 snaps. LJ Martin and Evan Johnson Officially Ruled Out for BYU Against ASU If Martin returns, it would be the first time BYU has had its full compliment of running backs since the season opener. Other Injury Updates on BYU Starters BYU also provided injury updates on key starters Roger Saleapaga and Evan Johnson. Saleapaga left the game against ASU with an injury, and Johnson suffered what appeared to be a serious ankle injury against UCF. Johnson did not play against Arizona State last weekend. Most of the time, BYU had three safeties on the field. BYU averaged 2.7 safeties on the field at a time against ASU. True freshman Kennan Pula has seen his role grow over the last few weeks. He played 24 snaps against the Sun Devils. away.headline: LJ Martin’s status looms large as BYU tries to fix its run game before Utah
away.blurb: Can LJ Martin return to help BYU's rushing attack against Utah? LJ Martin’s status looms large as BYU tries to fix its run game before Utah The Cougars’ rushing production has steadily declined since losing their star running back. His status remains uncertain heading into Saturday’s rivalry game. “Obviously, we got to look out for him first, and then we’ll just see if he does better tomorrow,” he added. “Hopefully, he doesn’t have any setbacks. We’ll just keep looking at him throughout the week.” Even if Martin can’t go, the Cougars (7-1, 4-1 Big 12) aren’t running away from the issues. They’re not even placing the burden of fixing those problems on backup running backs like Sione Moa — who recently returned from a second leg injury in the past year — or Preston Rex, who saw a noticeable uptick in carries against Iowa State and Notre Dame before sitting out against Arizona State. The offensive line is certainly feeling it, starting with position coach TJ Woods. The outspoken run-game coordinator has been blunt with his players in meetings, during film review, and in practice as BYU works to figure out its rushing ahead of Saturday’s rivalry game at third-ranked, undefeated Utah (10 a.m. MT, ABC). “One thing coach Woods does a great job of is keeping us accountable,” said veteran guard Sonny Makasini, the fifth-year senior out of Timpview High. “Whether it’s a good game or a bad game, he’s going to let us know what we messed up on. The Cougars needed just 4.03 yards per carry to stun then-No. 2 Notre Dame, getting a career game from the converted safety Rex with 66 yards on 10 carries. But one week later, the average dropped to 3.22 yards per rush in a double-overtime loss at UCF and bottomed out at 47 total rush yards and just 1.6 yards per carry in Saturday’s 27-20 win over the Sun Devils. Clearly, figuring out the run game has been a topic of conversation in the offensive line group chat. (Trent Nelson | The Salt Lake Tribune) BYU Cougars running back Lj Martin (4) as BYU hosts Arizona, NCAA football in Provo on Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026. Provo • There was no beating around the bush when BYU head coach Kalani Sitake and offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick watched the film from the Cougars’ 27-20 win over Arizona State last Saturday. The run game, or lack thereof, wasn’t a good look in the 7-point win over the Sun Devils. home.blurb: BYU Star LJ Martin Moving Closer to Return For Utah Game The No. 9 BYU Cougars are set to return Big 12 standout running back LJ Martin on Saturday against No. 3 Utah , according to multiple sources reporting that the senior is slated to dress. Martin moved up from “doubtful” to “questionable” on BYU's latest injury report for Week 10 at Utah, and, according to a Friday report by Pete Thamel at ESPN, Martin's spent the last three days actively participating in practice in hopes of seeing the field for Saturday's pivotal matchup that could shape the final three weeks of Big 12 football. Star tailback LJ Martin practiced the last three days for BYU. He’s on track to dress and attempt to play on Saturday. He’ll likely be limited, but he’s determined to impact the game. How he feels pre-game will determine extent of his role. https://t.co/Jaw1OsFKM3 Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today The Thamel report included that Martin is “determined to impact the game” on Saturday as the Cougars enter the matchup as a slight 4.5-point underdog . Martin's missed four consecutive weeks of football since enduring a lower-body injury during a 17-10 road win at TCU in early October. home.headline: BYU releases initial LJ Martin injury status ahead of Utah game
home.blurb: On Wednesday night, the BYU football program provided the first official injury update for LJ Martin ahead of a top 10 matchup with Utah. Martin is "doubtful" for the game against the Utes. The "doubtful" designation is reserved for the players that have a 25% chance to play. However, just a few minutes before the injury report came out, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Martin is considered "questionable" for this weekend. The "questionable" designation is reserved for players with a 50% chance to play. Thamel reported that if Martin returns, "he's not expected to be 100% and could be limited." Thamel added more information, saying "[Martin is] trending to dress, be available, and have some impact on the game. A final decision will be made later this week." Martin was back practicing on Tuesday, according to Aaron Roderick. The last time he played was in early October against TCU. If Martin can't go, BYU will turn to Preston Rex who was not available for the ASU game. Rex had a breakout game against Notre Dame before suffering an injury against UCF. If Saleapaga isn't available, expect more sets with three wide receivers. That would leave Walker Lyons on the field for most of the game. If Evan Johnson can't play, BYU will turn to Jayven Williams and Therrian Alexander III at cornerback. Williams and Alexander shut down two of the best wide receivers in the Big 12 last week. They are more than capable of holding it down on the outside. The bigger question will be who BYU plays at nickel. The Cougars started Cannon DeVries at that spot to start the season, but DeVries has primarily been used for punt return duties since he suffered an injury. The ASU game was the first time DeVries had seen defensive snaps since suffering the injury. He played 14 snaps. LJ Martin and Evan Johnson Officially Ruled Out for BYU Against ASU If Martin returns, it would be the first time BYU has had its full compliment of running backs since the season opener. Other Injury Updates on BYU Starters BYU also provided injury updates on key starters Roger Saleapaga and Evan Johnson. Saleapaga left the game against ASU with an injury, and Johnson suffered what appeared to be a serious ankle injury against UCF. Johnson did not play against Arizona State last weekend. Most of the time, BYU had three safeties on the field. BYU averaged 2.7 safeties on the field at a time against ASU. True freshman Kennan Pula has seen his role grow over the last few weeks. He played 24 snaps against the Sun Devils. The Tigers (6-2, 3-2 SEC) have already blown out league foes Florida and Texas A&M at home this season and are 13-3 at Faurot Field against league opposition since 2023. Taking on Texas (6-2, 3-2) represents an uptick in competition, but the Tigers shouldn't be lacking confidence. Florida was No. 8 in the AP poll when it arrived at Mizzou on Oct. 3. It left with a 45-17 loss that legitimized Missouri and showed its full potential. Since then, we've also seen Missouri's floor, which was found in a 31-3 loss at Ole Miss on Oct. 17. But after a bye week and a 34-10 "get right" win over Arkansas in Week 9, the Tigers appear to be back on track. The Longhorns are entering off wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State , but their vaunted offense is still falling short of expectations. Is this the point when everything will start to click for quarterback Arch Manning ? If a Texas team that spent four weeks at No. 1 earlier this season is going to meet expectations, a breakthrough needs to come soon. Texas vs. Missouri: Need to know Injuries mount for Texas: Injuries are adding up for the Longhorns, who enter this matchup with star receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman listed as questionable. Wingo is dealing with a quad injury while Coleman is working through a shoulder issue. Both have appeared in all eight games for Texas up to this point while combining to catch 11 of Arch Manning's 15 touchdown passes. Star edge rusher Collin Simmons is also questionable after missing Texas' past two games because of an ankle injury. That's a lot of star power in the "questionable" category for Texas. By contrast, Missouri's injury report is nearly clean. Welcome back, Ahmad: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy made his 2026 debut last week, carrying the football twice in the Tigers' win over Arkansas. The 2025 All-American has been on the mend from a gunshot wound, and his return adds to a running back room that already features the SEC's leading rusher. Jamal Roberts became the conference's first back to surpass 1,000 yards for the season while rushing for 138 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in a win over Arkansas. Roberts surpassed 200 yards in wins over Florida and Texas A&M last month. Gaining traction against Texas will be tough. No team has averaged more than four yards per rush attempt against Texas. College Football playoff implications: Texas' chance to reach the College Football Playoff will improve to 67.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFB Forecaster. They will drop to 22.8% with a loss. If the Longhorns lose, they would need to win out against LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M in order to potentially reach the 12-team field as a three-loss team. Missouri's chances to make the CFP will improve to 16.1% with a win. Those hopes would crater to 1.6% with a loss. The Tigers close with Georgia , Kentucky and Oklahoma . Regardless of the health status of star edge rusher Collin Simmons, the Longhorns should be able to slow down a Missouri offense that hasn't faced a swarming unit of this caliber. picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Predicts Missouri Upset That Could Shake Texas' Playoff Hopes Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy believes Texas’ turnover problems will catch up with the Longhorns at Missouri, making the Tigers his lone outright upset pick of Week 10 as both 6-2 SEC teams fight to stay in the College Football Playoff race. McElroy backed the Tigers on his Always College Football podcast, predicting a low-scoring game decided by ball security. “The team that gives it away just one time, that’s the team that’s going to lose,” he said. Why is Greg McElroy picking Missouri? Missouri Tigers head coach Eli Drinkwitz reacts toward a referee during the first quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “Missouri is +8 in turnover margin. Texas is -3,” McElroy said. “That’s probably the clearest season-long difference between these two teams.” “Missouri is +8 in turnover margin. Texas is -3,” McElroy said. “That’s probably the clearest season-long difference between these two teams.” The Tigers turned four Arkansas turnovers into 24 points in last week’s win in Fayetteville, and Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz said afterward that “turnovers are the name of the game .” McElroy added that Missouri has scored 62 points off takeaways this season without allowing a point off a giveaway. “So when his team wins the turnover battle by one or more, Eli Drinkwitz is 39-4,” McElroy said. Texas checked in at No. 7 in the first College Football Playoff rankings , 11 spots ahead of Missouri. Still, both Missouri losses came on the road against Mississippi State and Ole Miss, two teams Texas beat over the last two weeks. Arch Manning’s costly turnover trouble Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) looks on after a medical check during the game against Ole Miss | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Texas quarterback Arch Manning has 15 touchdown passes and averages 8 yards per attempt, but McElroy flagged his seven interceptions as a problem against a team that “cashes mistakes in very, very quickly.” Both Texas losses came by three points and turned on fourth-quarter turnovers, including a pick-six against Oklahoma and a strip-sack with under two minutes left against Florida. Texas quarterback Arch Manning has 15 touchdown passes and averages 8 yards per attempt, but McElroy flagged his seven interceptions as a problem against a team that “cashes mistakes in very, very quickly.” Both Texas losses came by three points and turned on fourth-quarter turnovers, including a pick-six against Oklahoma and a strip-sack with under two minutes left against Florida. Mississippi State sacked the redshirt junior six times last Saturday, and Texas now plays without left tackle Trevor Goosby, who suffered a season-ending knee injury against Ole Miss. “They average getting sacked nearly one out of every 10 dropbacks,” McElroy said of Texas. “That’s 126th because the breakdowns come from all over the protection.” The ESPN analyst said Texas has struggled when its receivers have to beat man coverage snap after snap, and he called Missouri’s cornerbacks “about as good as you find when it comes to playing that coverage week in and week out.” How does Texas reach 24 points? Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian celebrates with fans and players after the game against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy questioned how Texas coach Steve Sarkisian’s offense gets there. “When his team scores fewer than 24 points, Steve Sarkisian is 14-35,” McElroy said. “And Texas already goes three-and-out on more than a quarter of their possessions.” McElroy questioned how Texas coach Steve Sarkisian’s offense gets there. “When his team scores fewer than 24 points, Steve Sarkisian is 14-35,” McElroy said. “And Texas already goes three-and-out on more than a quarter of their possessions.” The Longhorns’ running game offers little relief, with McElroy saying their backs “are getting hit almost as soon as they take the handoff.” Running back Hollywood Smothers is out, and receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman were both listed as questionable on Thursday’s SEC availability report . Wingo, a St. Louis native Missouri recruited out of high school, leads Texas with 36 catches for 470 yards, while Coleman, an Auburn transfer, leads the team with seven touchdown catches. McElroy’s route to 24 points runs through Wingo “in the catch-and-run game” against a Missouri defense he said sits “at or near the bottom as far as missed tackles,” plus “one Coleman shot over the top.” “But without it, Texas might be living on field goals, which is a dangerous recipe on the road,” McElroy said. A loss would send Texas to LSU next week with three defeats, a scenario ESPN analyst Paul Finebaum said could cause the Longhorns to “ collapse .” Texas visits Missouri at noon ET Saturday on ESPN. picks.blurb: Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas vs. Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas vs. Missouri Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 7 Texas and No. 18 Missouri have only met once on the football field since the Tigers left the Big 12 along side Texas A&M for the SEC. That meeting was the 2017 Texas Bowl. What should scare Longhorns fans is the 2026 version is tinkering on the edge of a disappointing bowl like that. Especially if they can't beat a team like Missouri. The Tigers are a good team. It's easy to see Missouri winning on Saturday. They're ranked just 11 spots below Texas in the College Football Playoff rankings and have the same record. And Mizzou has home field advantage. Then why is Texas a -3.5-point favorite. Because a fully functioning Texas team is better than Missouri. But this Texas team isn't fully functioning. First, the injuries are starting to pile up. It was announced this week that the Longhorns have lost running back Hollywood Smothers and tight end Nick Townsend for the rest of the season. All-American right tackle Trevor Goosby is also out for the year. And UT has been without All-American EDGE Colin Simmons for weeks. In addition to trying to plug the injury holes, Texas coach Steve Sarkisian must also continue to work on the offense. At times it looks great. But its not trustworthy. Will Muschamp's defense will need to stand tall for a third game in a row if the offense can't get it going. Tommy Bresee's Prediction Texas walks into this Missouri game needing the win to feel confident about their CFP chance heading into LSU. Missouri is a relative unknown, with losses to both Mississippi schools but a dominating win over Florida. Jamal Roberts and the run game leads the way, averaging just over 160 rushing yards/game. Austin Simmons has become a riser in this upcoming NFL Draft, flashing his elite arm talent every week. Texas was able to get a win over Tennessee earlier this season, but I don't see this as a task that's comparable. Missouri is capable of performing at a high level on both sides of the ball, especially the front seven defensively. It's difficult to imagine this Texas offense to trade punches with Missouri, especially on the road, so I'll take the Tigers to possibly end Texas' CFP hopes. Final Score: Texas 20, Missouri 23 Jamie Gatlin's Prediction The Longhorns will take on Missouri this Saturday in their latest SEC clash. The Tigers are off to an impressive 6-2 start and, like Texas, are 3-2 in conference play. Texas will need Arch Manning to be at his best and for the defense to shine. Last week, the Longhorns defense held Mississippi State to three points and 187 total yards. If the Longhorns can replicate that performance, another win could be on the horizon. This should be a game that Texas can win as they look to improve their playoff odds. Final Score: Texas 31, Missouri 13 Trey Luerssen's Prediction When this year's schedule came out, I thought the game against Mizzou might be the toughest to forecast. But it's even tougher now, because we're not sure which team will actually show up on either side of the ball. Both teams have had some big wins and some real clunkers. How much will Texas miss Smothers and Townsend? Can the defense slow down the Tigers offense? Which version of quarterback Arch Manning will show up in Columbia? For four games in a row, Texas has jumped out to an early lead and then coughed it up by the end of the third quarter. UT is 2-2 in that stretch. A coin flip. Twice the dam broke and twice it didn't. I think the defense will save the offense again. Mandatory Credit: Brett Rojo-Imagn Images (Brett Rojo/IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) PJ Green · Kansas City Star Mon, November 2, 2026 at 8:17 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The No. 19 Missouri Tigers will begin a treacherous final month of SEC play Saturday when the No. 10 Texas Longhorns come to Columbia. With two losses apiece, there will be College Football Playoff ramifications from this game. The first ranking is set to be released Tuesday evening, which also could cause the betting lines to move. As it currently sits, the Tigers will host the Longhorns where they are the slimmest underdog they have been all season. Take a look at the betting line and game prediction... Missouri vs. Texas: Betting line Odds via bet365 Missouri: +2.5 (-102) Texas: -2.5 (-118) Missouri-Texas moneyline Missouri: +124 O/U 44.5 (-110) Mizzou vs. Texas game prediction After back-to-back losses to Oklahoma and Florida, Texas got back on track with wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State to end October. The Longhorns' storylines have been dominated by their underwhelming Arch Manning-led offense, but they've put together enough quality performances to be a top-10 team. Injuries to potential top NFL Draft picks OT Trevor Goosby and DE Colin Simmons have hurt Texas, but haven't held it back. Missouri bounced back from a drubbing at Ole Miss to give the same treatment to Arkansas on the road. The Tigers look like a healthier squad that's ready to make a push to national prominence during the final stage of the season. This game would be a tossup at a neutral site, but home-field advantage favors Missouri. The Tigers are undefeated at Memorial Stadium this season. In MU's two losses, it was beaten by two elite performances from dynamic quarterbacks while the Tigers' offense couldn't keep up. It would likely take the same for the Longhorns to leave Columbia with a win. Missouri hasn't had to play a game that goes down to the wire yet this season. This could be it. Score prediction: Missouri wins 27-25

Now, the No. 10 Longhorns (6-2, 3-2 SEC) hope two straight victories away from Austin can solidify a spot in the College Football Playoff standings This video created with the assistance of AI. The tricky road trip begins Saturday against No. 19 Missouri and extends to Nov. 14 against No. 15 LSU. But Texas, listed at No. 7 in this week's CFP rankings , can't afford to look past a rugged Missouri squad that likes to run the ball and lean on its defense. The beat-up Longhorns have lost All-American left tackle Trevor Goosby for the season and must overcome a rash of other injuries entering Saturday's game. Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Missouri Tigers. GOLDEN: Defense is Texas' pathway to playoff, but Arch Manning's legs are useful, too | Golden No. 10 Texas (6-2, 3-2 SEC) at No. 19 Missouri (6-2, 3-2) When: 11 a.m. Saturday Where: Faurot Field in Columbia, Miss. TV/radio: ESPN, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: Pack a jacket, because temperatures could be in the low 40s at kickoff and won't climb out of the 50s. But rain chances look slight and the Midwest winds should be gentle on a perfect day for football. Texas vs Missouri football betting info Moneyline: Texas -145/ Missouri +120 Spread: Texas is favored by 3 points. Over/under : 46½ Texas history: Missouri All-time: Texas leads 18-6 Last meeting: Texas 33, Missouri 16 (2017) Most memorable meeting: Texas 56, Missouri 31 (Oct. 18, 2008). Former coach Gary Pinkel turned Missouri into a Big 12 contender in the 2000s, but the Tigers could never get over the hump against a Texas squad in the heart of its golden era under Mack Brown . They came closest in 2008, when Missouri quarterback Chase Daniel and Texas quarterback Colt McCoy combined for 655 yards passing. McCoy accounted for four total touchdowns for a Texas team that went 12-1 but missed out on a chance to play for a national championship after a wrenching last-second loss at Texas Tech in Week 9. Texas defensive lineman Maraad Watson (88) returns a fumble for a touchdown during the game against Mississippi State at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Know the foe: Missouri Last week: Beat Arkansas, 34-10 Players to watch: QB Austin Simmons , a 6-foot-4, 220-pound senior, once seemed like the heir apparent at Ole Miss but transferred to Missouri this past offseason after the emergence of current Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss. He's averaging 244 yards passing a game on 63.3% passing with 17 passing touchdowns compared to just two interceptions. RB Jamal Roberts , a 6-foot, 215-pound senior, stepped into a starring role after All-SEC running back Ahmad Hardy got shot in the leg at a concert in May and missed the first seven games of this season following surgery. Roberts leads the SEC with 1,005 yards rushing and averages 5.3 yards per carry. LB Nicholas Rodriguez, a 6-foot, 225-pound junior, leads the SEC with 11 tackles and game and forced a fumble in last week's win over Arkansas. His sideline-to-sideline range anchors the Tiger run defense. Central Texas connections: None. When Texas has the ball The Longhorns have issues running the ball, and Missouri prides itself on stopping the run. The ground game doesn't seem like a recipe for Longhorn success, especially since Texas running backs Hollywood Smothers and Derrek Cooper remain limited by injuries. Longhorn RB Raleek Brown followed up a 157-yard game against Ole Miss with just 30 yards rushing in last week's win over Mississippi State, and Missouri ranks third in SEC play by allowing only 104.8 yards rushing a game. Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) runs the ball during the game against Mississippi State at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Missouri ranks just 12 th in the SEC with 11 sacks in league play, but the Longhorns have struggled to protect QB Arch Manning while allowing 20 sacks in five SEC games. If a revamped Texas line with two tackles in new positions in right tackle Andre Cojoe and left tackle Melvin Siani can give Manning time, he may exploit a Tiger defense that gives up 260.4 yards passing a game in league play. When Missouri has the ball The Tigers like to pound the ball, especially since Hardy made his season debut last week against Arkansas. If Hardy can find the form that helped him rush for 3,000 yards and 29 TDs over his first two collegiate seasons, he'll team with Roberts in arguably the best backfield in college football. But Texas gives up yards on the ground grudgingly; the defense allows just 98.4 yards per game rushing in SEC play, which ranks only behind Georgia. The secondary may be the most beat-up unit on the squad, which is saying something for the bruised and battered Longhorns. Graceson Littleton , an elite slot corner, will likely miss the game. So could starting cornerback Kade Phillips. Texas could compensate by moving top corner Bo Mascoe to the slot, which is a critical position for the Longhorns' defense that ranks 10 th in the nation with 273.1 yards allowed per game MORE: How tight ends, backs can help the worst passing game in the Sarkisian-era Texas vs Missouri key matchup Texas cornerback Warren Roberson vs. Missouri receiver Cayden Lee Veteran Warren Roberson, who has played in 36 career games for the Longhorns, could get his first career start for the Longhorns' banged-up corners. It's a daunting debut, since Missouri's Cayden Lee leads the SEC with 756 yards receiving on 53 catches. Texas vs Missouri prediction Thomas Jones: Missouri 23, Texas 20. Texas has a history of playing well in big games under head coach Steve Sarkisian, but can the Longhorns find the needed emotional spark in their first conference visit to this SEC hinterlands? It's the game of the year for many Mizzou fans; it feels like a trap for Texas. Danny Davis: Texas. The Longhorns are solidly back in the CFP conversation and will remain so even if the defense has to carry them to another win this weekend in Columbia as injuries and inefficiencies continue to haunt the UT offense. Cedric Golden: Texas 24, Missouri 21. The Longhorns are beaten up and understand how essential this win will be to their postseason hopes. They have a much better chance of beating Missouri than they do of winning at LSU next week. They take advantage and eek out a win, thanks again to the defense. Michael Shapiro: Texas 20, Missouri 19. Texas' defense will stiffen in the red zone against a strong Missouri run game, and Arch Manning will continue to churn yards on the ground in a grinding, just-effective-enough afternoon for the Longhorns' offense. This is life in the SEC. It might not be pretty, but every win is another point of evidence for Steve Sarkisian as he makes Texas' case for inclusion in the College Football Playoff. picks.headline: Missouri football vs Texas scouting report, score prediction for top-20 game
picks.blurb: It’s Tigers versus Longhorns in a top-20 battle. No. 19-ranked Missouri football will take on No. 9/10 Texas this coming Saturday, Nov. 7, on Faurot Field in a top-20 matchup that will have significant implications on the College Football Playoff race in the SEC. Mizzou (6-2, 3-2 SEC) doesn’t have much more — if any — margin for error this year, and Eli Drinkwitz looks likely to have essentially his full roster available for the huge home game. Texas (6-2, 3-2) is coming off back-to-back wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State, which were MU’s two losses this year, and holds the No. 7 ranking in the initial CFP top 25. Here’s what Mizzou fans need to know about the Longhorns, as well as a score prediction for the Nov. 7 game: How does Missouri defend Texas QB Arch Manning? Mizzou has to get consistent pressure on Arch Manning. No quarterback in the SEC has been sacked as many times as Manning. No QB has thrown as many passes considered “turnover-worthy,” at least in Pro Football Focus’ accounting, while under pressure than the Texas QB’s seven. There’s been a boom-or-bust element to Manning’s play when rushers get into his space. Not only has he thrown seven turnover-worthy passes on those plays, but he’s thrown an SEC-high nine “Big Time Throws.” Quite often, he’s taking a shot with some degree of difficulty or deep downfield when pressure arrives at his doorstep. Perhaps more importantly, though, will be coverage sacks. Manning is happy to wait for routes to develop, even if it means he’s taking a hit. The longer the Tigers’ defensive backs can stay attached to their assignments, giving the QB fewer options to bail the offense out with big throws, the better. Can Mizzou keep turnover margin in its favor? Missouri keeps winning the turnover battle. The Tigers are averaging a +1.3 turnover margin per game this year, which is tied for the sixth-best mark nationally. Texas, meanwhile, is 94th in the country, giving the ball away more per game than it is taking it away. The Longhorns, at -2.0, actually have the third-worst turnover margin in the FBS in road games this year. Manning has recorded the eighth-most fumbles in the country this season. He’s also thrown seven picks, three of which were while he was under pressure, per PFF. There aren’t many stats that translate to winning football games like creating and avoiding turnovers. “Turnovers are the name of the game,” Drinkwitz said after MU’s win at Arkansas, where his team forced four. Texas has been a little prone to giveaways, so the more hits the Tigers can land on Manning, probably the better. Texas injury concerns The Longhorns’ injury report had a number of notable names Wednesday night to open the gameweek. Three defensive starters were listed as questionable, including star defensive end and future first-rounder Colin Simmons. Texas also listed starting nickel Graceson Littleton and corner Kade Phillips as questionable to face Mizzou. Two starting wide receivers join those players on the 50/50 list: Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman. The Longhorns have ruled out rotational running back Hollywood Smothers and starting left tackle Trevor Goosby. Is this a CFP elimination game? The first College Football Playoff rankings of the 2026 season arrived Tuesday with Mizzou checking in at No. 18 and Texas at No. 7. That gives us a good idea of what the committee thinks of two teams that have identical records (6-2, 3-2 SEC). The Tigers need some quality wins — and fast. They’ll get chances. In the next three weeks, Drinkwitz’s team faces CFP-ranked No. 7 Texas, No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Kentucky. It’s possible that a 9-3 team from the SEC sneaks into the playoff. Likely, at this point. But is it Mizzou? The path to that record, which at least puts MU in the conversation, probably requires a win over Texas. Georgia on the road, after all, is next. That ain’t easy. Texas at No. 7 is a different story. It’s tough to tell exactly what the committee is thinking, but checking in that high says that the committee values wins over Ohio State, Tennessee and Ole Miss. The Longhorns could maybe afford a loss to MU, provided it then turns around and beats LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M down the stretch. There’s a lot of football to play, but this is a fascinating game in the scope of the year. Score prediction: Missouri 24, Texas 20 This game could come down to how well Mizzou runs the football. The Texas defense has elite athletes up front, even if players like Simmons can’t go, and the Tigers cannot afford to struggle on the ground like they did against Ole Miss. If that happens, the Longhorns are running away with this one. But if Jamal Roberts and Ahmad Hardy can help MU control the clock and open up some space for Austin Simmons through the air, the Tigers have a really good chance for a memorable day at Memorial Stadium.

away.headline: Texas' Hollywood Smothers Reportedly Out for Rest of CFB Season with Knee Injury
away.blurb: Smothers wasn't available for games against Tennessee and Ole Miss, and he has been an ineffective option as part of a rotation with running back Raleek Brown. Smothers carried the ball just four times for minus-6 yards before entering the medical tent against Mississippi State last week. Texas running back Hollywood Smothers will miss the remainder of the 2026 season with a torn MCL, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported. Smothers was among the top running backs in the 2026 transfer class after rushing for 939 yards with seven touchdowns at NC State last season. He was expected to be an explosive addition to the Longhorns offense and began the season as the starting running back, but he has been hampered by injuries throughout the season. The Longhorns entered the season with high expectations, but inconsistent performances from quarterback Arch Manning and a bevy of injuries have threatened to derail their campaign. Texas was ranked No. 1 after starting the season with a 4-0 record, but they now sit as the No. 7 ranked team after two consecutive losses against unranked Oklahoma and Florida. Texas will need Brown to carry a larger workload as they fight to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive moving forward, but the injuries are continuing to mount. The Longhorns have already lost star left tackle Trevor Goosby to a season-ending injury, and the team's injury report for their upcoming game against Missouri is nearly as long as a drug store receipt. Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian will need players to step up in order for the team to live up to their preseason expectations. The margin for error is slim, and those injuries could prove to be critical during their upcoming road games against two ranked opponents, No. 18 Missouri and No. 14 LSU. away.blurb: The Texas Longhorns have been bitten by the injury bug and there are some big names on the SEC availability report . Now, running back Hollywood Smothers and tight end Nick Townsend are out for the game at Missouri. Smothers reportedly hurt his knee and shoulder against the Bulldogs. Townsend is a bit of a surprise. Wide receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman were both in street clothes on the sideline by the end of the game against Hail State. Both are listed as questionable. away.blurb: Missouri football's injury report was unchanged from last week on the SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report with Malae Fonoti, Josh Atkins and Gavin Hoffman all listed as out. The Tigers' opponent, the Texas Longhorns, had a much more extensive list that included five starters listed as questionable. Star edge rusher Colin Simmons headlines the list of questionable Longhorns after missing the last two games. Despite not playing since Oct. 17, Simmons leads the country with 10.5 sacks. Running back Hollywood Smothers and tight end Nick Townsend were listed as out after playing last week against Mississippi State. Smothers, who suffered an injury against the Bulldogs, is second in rushing yards on the Longhorns, leaving the bulk of carries to Raleek Brown. Townsend, who has been dealing with an ongoing injury, has started three games this season and recorded two catches and four yards last week. Of the remaining Longhorns, Trevor Goosby is out for the season and Richard Wesley has been out since Oct. 17. The Tigers (6-2, 3-2 Southeastern Conference) are looking to become the first ranked team to defeat No. 7 Texas (6-2, 3-2) this season, after the Longhorns have gone 3-0 against ranked opponents. If Missouri comes out on top, it would be its second top-10 victory of the season. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/missouri as 5 Texas starters listed as questionable ahead of contest against Mizzou football . The other two most notable names on the injury report are the Longhorns' top receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman. Wingo has appeared in every game up to this point and leads the Longhorns in receptions (36) and receiving yards (470) and has added a team-second four receiving touchdowns. Coleman has appeared in every contest as well, is third in receiving yards (409) and leads the team with seven receiving touchdowns. In the secondary, the Longhorns could be without two big names in starting defensive backs Kade Phillips and Graceson Littleton. Phillips has started in all eight games and Littleton has started in seven contests. Phillips ranks fifth in the team in tackles (34) and is tied for third in pass breakups with four, while Littleton has logged 28 tackles and ranks second with five pass breakups. On the Tigers end, the three players listed last week were the same on Wednesday's report, signaling that Ahmad Hardy will be making his home debut Saturday.
