LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 5 Alabama is out to defend its College Football Playoff ranking, while No. 14 LSU seeks to remain in the hunt Getty Images One of the most exciting modern rivalries in college football takes center stage on Saturday when No. 5 Alabama and No. 14 LSU meet in Baton Rouge for the 91st meeting in the series. The Crimson Tide hold a 58-27-5 advantage overall, but it's the 13-2 record in the past 15 meetings that has given them the upper hand in a battle between programs that would otherwise be considered peers. This is, after all, set to be the 25th time that both schools are inside the top 15 of the AP Top 25 poll and with Alabama's recent crowning as a top-five team in the College Football Playoff rankings, there's even more ranked-on-ranked intrigue. LSU is hoping that the home field advantage of Death Valley can play a role in the game, as the Tigers are 32-3 in their last 35 home games in Tiger Stadium. Speaking of streaks, the game also presents LSU coach Lane Kiffin with a chance to finally defeat Alabama as a head coach. The former Crimson Tide offensive coordinator lost to Nick Saban once as Tennessee's head coach in 2009, then four times between 2020-23 as Ole Miss ' head coach, when they were SEC West division rivals. That 0-5 record against the Crimson Tide, paired with LSU's recent struggles in the series, provides plenty of extra motivation for the home team looking to roar back into the playoff race. Alabama vs. LSU: Need to know Alabama's injury report will be an X-factor: There will be key updates throughout the week, perhaps all the way up to warm-ups, that will determine the health of the Crimson Tide and their ability to perform to the expectations of their top-five rating. Starting center Racin Delgatty has missed multiple games while dealing with injury, and his absence has been noticeable on an offensive line that has cooled off since putting up 49+ points in consecutive wins against Florida State , South Carolina and Mississippi State . The Crimson Tide have failed to record 70+ rushing yards as a team in each of their last two games and allowed 21 sacks in SEC play, which ranks 14th among 16 teams in the league. Alabama will also be looking for updates from star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and cornerback Zabien Brown , adding to the unknowns for how the Tide will stack up against LSU. LSU passing attack rounding into form : No one in the SEC had a more productive passing attack in the month of October than LSU, which averaged 339.5 passing yards across all four games last month. The Tigers went 3-1 across those games, only losing to top-10 Kentucky by one point in Lexington on a walk-off two-point try. LSU now leads the SEC and ranks tied for 7th nationally on the season, averaging 318.0 passing yards per game, and the improvements have come with both Sam Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris as a go-to receiver. A transfer from Hawaii , Harris played three whole games before scoring his first touchdown of the season but has exploded ever since with seven touchdown catches across the last five games. That includes four multiple-touchdown games and a yards-per-reception average (17.6) that ranks 4th among all SEC pass catchers. Kalen DeBoer set up in some favorable situational spots : When Alabama hired Kalen DeBoer away from Washington to take over in Tuscaloosa after Nick Saban's retirement, his track record as a big-time, high-leverage coach met the demands of the job. Since Alabama is almost always playing in high-pressure games against quality opponents, the school needed to know that Saban's successor would be ready for those moments. Currently, DeBoer is 21-8 against AP-ranked teams as a head coach, which is the fourth-best record in AP poll history with a minimum of 20 games coached (.724 winning percentage). His company on that list, for those unaware, is one spot behind Urban Meyer (.746) and one spot ahead of Kirby Smart (.710). DeBoer has also won eight straight games after a bye, with the last defeat in this spot coming in 2020 as the head coach of Fresno State . Where to watch Alabama vs. LSU live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Tiger Stadium -- Baton Rouge, Louisiana TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Alabama vs. LSU prediction, picks While the combination of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell provides the potential for plenty of points, this game could end up being decided by both defenses. Alabama's offensive injuries have clearly limited their ability to execute on schedule, and LSU's defense represents the best test they've faced since the loss at Tennessee. In the same manner, LSU's pass attack could set them up for some of the turnovers that have powered Alabama's excellence this season (+7 turnover margin is tied for 11th nationally) and prevent touchdowns even after successful drives. All in all, it points to a lower-scoring classic, where I'll favor the home team to make big plays late. Alabama looks to win its fourth straight Saban Bowl on the first Saturday in November when the Crimson Tide take on LSU at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La., at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC). The Tigers are 5.5-point favorites in Death Valley, and my Alabama vs. LSU prediction and college football picks are backing Lane Kiffin to end the losing streak. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs LSU: LSU -5.5 The last time LSU won the Saban Bowl, Nick Saban was Alabama's head coach and Lane Kiffin was still beloved at Ole Miss . That will change Saturday when Kiffin's surging Tigers take advantage of a Crimson Tide team that's looked like a far cry from its No. 5 College Football Playoff ranking. With LSU's defensive ferocity and Alabama's offensive struggles, I like the Tigers to cover up to -6.5 at home against the Tide. Not only has LSU's defense been wrecking opponents, but the Tigers' offense has been on fire too, with Sam Leavitt fourth nationally in QBR (85.3) and 12th in adjusted completion percentage (79.5%). Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris (480 receiving yards and seven TDs in his last four SEC games) are a problem for an Alabama defense that's ranked 78th in pass success rate (44.3%). Alabama vs LSU Over/Under pick: Under 52.5 This game isn't one of the must-watch games in my college football Top 25 predictions this week because I'm expecting offensive fireworks; it's because of the talent on these defenses. LSU's defense is especially loaded, and with Alabama's struggles against quality defenses, I would play the Under at 51.5 or better. The Tigers are second nationally in sacks (34) , and Keelon Russell hasn't managed pressure well. He's been sacked the ninth-most in the country (22) and has a 20.4% pressure-to-sack rate. But I don't expect an offensive onslaught from LSU either. This is the best defense the Tigers have faced this season, with Alabama ranking 20th nationally in available yards percentage (37.7%) and 14th in net adjusted EPA per play. Alabama vs LSU combo Alabama has gotten off to slow starts and failed to cover in three straight games as a result. In the Crimson Tide's last three games, it trailed Georgia 10-0, trailed Tennessee 9-0, and trailed Texas A&M 14-10. If Alabama gets off to another slow start and trails LSU, the Tigers' defense will pin their ears back and go to work. LSU ranks eighth nationally in pass success rate on defense (36%) and has one of the most lethal pass rush duos in the country, Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross (58 combined pressures and 13.5 sacks). Death Valley is one of the hardest places to play, and with Alabama's broken offense, I don't expect the Tide to score much early against this opportunistic LSU defense. A team which Alabama has won the last three games against dating back to 2023, this latest showdown against LSU is likely to be their toughest in recent years. The Tigers are considered one of the SEC's top teams at 6-2 (3-2 SEC), and have a roster loaded with talent led by head coach Lane Kiffin. In addition to that, this latest matchup between the Crimson Tide and Tigers has significant College Football Playoff (CFP) implications. Released this past Tuesday night, Alabama was ranked No. 5 in the first CFP rankings as the top ranked two-loss team, while LSU sat at No. 14. A challenging matchup, let's make three predictions for the Crimson Tide during Saturday's massive road game at LSU. Alabama's offensive line struggles against LSU pass rush Oct 3, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide offensive lineman Michael Carroll (64) waits for the snap during the third quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. As a result, combined with the tough road atmosphere in Tiger Stadium, I'll predict the Alabama offensive line to struggle at times in pass protection against an elite LSU pass rush, especially if the Crimson Tide are without two starters up front. Alabama's defense forces multiple turnovers Oct 10, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide defensive back Bray Hubbard (18) celebrates his interception during the second quarter against the Georgia Bulldogs at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Keelon Russell, Tide passing game has solid showing While I do predict Alabama's offense to struggle in pass protection at times similar to the Tennessee game, I do not think the passing game will struggle as much as it did in Knoxville where the Tide threw for only 147 yards. Yes, the Tide are facing a LSU defense that ranks No. 3 in the SEC in fewest yards allowed per game, but Alabama might be getting Ryan Coleman-Williams back Saturday, and with an extra week of rest and preparation, I would imagine we see a different performance from Keelon Russell and company. The loser of this game may miss out on the college football playoff and given the Tigers' remaining strength of schedule, this is a must-win for LSU. Both teams are coming off a bye week, so we should expect a chess match between Lane Kiffin and Kalen DeBoer . Some would say this is a must-win for Alabama despite being the #5 ranked team in the new playoff rankings. The Tide's two best wins came against Kentucky when the Wildcats were unranked and a routing of #16 Mississippi State which sent Kamario Taylor and the program into a spiral. A win at LSU would solidify Alabama's spot, but a loss puts their season in the hands of others. Alabama plays Vanderbilt, Chattanooga, and Auburn following LSU; one of the easiest strength of schedules in P4. Alabama trailed 20-17 to Texas A&M before rattling off 14 points in the fourth quarter to avoid three-straight losses. Keelon Russell threw for 311 yards and three touchdowns, and the defense forced three turnovers in the win. Alabama has won three straight against LSU and won 12 of the last 15. Sam Leavitt and Kiffin will try to break the streak in his debut season. LSU is coming off two back-to-back big wins before the bye week. The Tigers crushed Mississippi State 31-0 and Auburn 38-17. Sam Leavitt threw seven touchdowns and ran for another in that two-game span, plus Jackson Harris caught four of those touchdowns and totaled 263 receiving yards. LSU's defense has only allowed 281 yards through the air in those two games as well, so nothing should come easy in Death Valley for one of the best home defenses in the country. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Alabama's offense has been without Ryan Coleman-Williams , so Scott has been one of the players asked to step up. Scott caught a career-high six passes for 156 yards and a season-long 48-yard reception. Russell threw for 311 yards, but the rushing attack struggled with 2.4 yards per carry on 28 carries for 68 yards. Alabama Player to Watch on Offense: QB Keelon Russell Keelon Russell had a bounce-back performance against Texas A&M. Russell threw two touchdowns in the fourth quarter to pull the Tide up, then seal the deal. He finished with 311 passing yards, three touchdowns, and one interception on 19-of-30. Alabama has been without Ryan Coleman-Williams for the last two games (TENN, TX A&M), but he could return this week, which would significantly boost Russell's output. The Alabama Crimson Tide Defense: Alabama's defense forced three turnovers last week: two interceptions and one fumble (forced three). The Tide held the Aggies to 278 total yards and 2.9 yards per rush, which is light-years better than the 150 rushing yards and 3.7 yards per carry allowed to Tennessee. In the last three games, Alabama allowed 20, 26, and 20 points, but were outgained in yards in their two losses to Tennessee and Georgia. Alabama Player to Watch on Defense: LB Caleb Woodson In the last three games, Caleb Woodson has racked up the tackles. He had nine versus Georgia, 11 at Tennessee, and 10 against Texas A&M for 30 of his team-leading 63 tackles. Woodson has four games with double-digit tackles this season after having one in three seasons with Virginia Tech. Woodson's career-high is 72 tackles, which he will likely pass this weekend, and another sack (2) or interception (1), and he will have career highs in both categories. Expect to hear Woodson's name early and often. The Tigers have found a balance between Dilin Jones and Sam Leavitt . Jones has 39 total carries in the last two games for 175 yards, and he's also caught 12 passes for 85 yards, for 51 total touches compared to 83 dropbacks for Leavitt. Jackson Harris has also caught four touchdowns and put up 263 yards in the last two games, so the stars have been shining for LSU. LSU Player to Watch on Offense: QB Sam Leavitt Sam Leavitt might be playing his best football of the season. In the last two games, Leavitt has thrown seven passing touchdowns with no picks and a rushing touchdown. In his first six games of the season, he had at least one pick in all of them, so this is a pleasant surprise for LSU. Leavitt has 25 total touchdowns on the year (17 pass, 8 rush) and will be a handful in this game with his dual-threat ability. Alabama has only allowed two quarterbacks to throw for two-plus touchdowns on their defense this season, and Leavitt has accomplished that in five straight games. If LSU wants to win, Leavitt will have to be on his A-game, and he went into the bye week on fire. The LSU Tigers Defense: At home, LSU's defense has allowed 10, 14, 6, 14, and 0 points for 8.8 points per game! That's one of the best marks in the country, and lately, the Tigers have played their best ball with 17 points allowed over the last two games and 140.5 passing yards per game. LSU has only forced one turnover in that dominant two-game stretch, and the Tigers will likely need to win the turnover battle to beat Alabama. LSU's defense ranks fifth in pressure and first in coverage grades per PFF, and with the Tide ranking 54th in pass blocking, LSU could find success getting to Keelon Russell . LSU Player to Watch on Defense: DE Princewill Umanmielen Princewill Umanmielen got back in this sack column against Auburn! While it was only a half-sack, it still counts toward his team-leading 8.5 sacks that ranks third in the country. Umanmielen's 12 TFLs rank tied eighth in the nation, and he ranks second in the SEC in both TFLs and sacks. He trails only Texas' Collin Simmons (16 TFLs, 10 sacks). LSU will host Alabama this upcoming Saturday in what's a de facto College Football Playoff elimination game. Alabama and LSU both have two losses. It's possible that the loser of this game could still get into the playoff with three losses — it depends on how the rest of the season plays out — but the winner will be the only one that controls its own destiny moving forward. ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, made his score prediction for the game, and he has LSU leaving Tiger Stadium with a 27-20 win. McElroy thinks LSU's defensive line will be able to win the battle up front. "I'm taking LSU to win the game 27-20," said McElroy. "I do think the under is in play, but it's really going to come down to Alabama's offensive line. If Keelon Russell gets time, they can win this game in Baton Rouge. But if they don't get time, it's going to be a real uphill climb for the Crimson Tide." McElroy noted that most of the sacks Alabama has given up this season have come from Russell holding the ball too long. Alabama and LSU will kick off at 2:30 PM CT/3:30 PM ET on Saturday. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) | Getty Images Joshua Chatham · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 3:18 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Happy Friday, everyone. The women's basketball team feasted on yet another cupcake last night to move to 3-0, this time taking down Alabama A&M by a 96-43 margin . The men play tonight against Arkansas State, and we will have coverage of that one later on. Alabama football plays at LSU tomorrow, as you well know. Your previews: Alabama gets an immediate chance to justify its CFP ranking, while LSU can strengthen its argument with a win that leaves the Tide staring at three losses. I picked LSU to win this game in August, and I'm sticking with the Tigers' passing game at home against an Alabama secondary still sorting through injuries. Sam Leavitt throws for 278 yards and two touchdowns, and Jackson Harris catches both of them while finishing with 110 receiving yards. LSU wins 26-20, keeping its SEC title hopes alive and giving Alabama fans another reason to avoid the internet. Alabama football needs this win. Kalen DeBoer wins after idle weeks. And the Crimson Tide knows how to win against LSU on the road. All of these remain true. But this is a new Tigers team in a new era with Lane Kiffin at the helm. It's a unit starting to find itself after single-score losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky. LSU has the second best scoring offense and defense in the SEC. It has the No. 1 total offense and defense in the SEC. This is a Tigers team that is waiting for an opportunity to see what it can do against the upper echelon of SEC play in November, and the Crimson Tide is the first team in LSU's way. Alabama has looked like the best team in the country before on the road, beating Mississippi State to a pulp in Starkville, but the same couldn't be said about Kentucky in Lexington, or, especially, Tennessee in Knoxville. Expect the Crimson Tide to falter against LSU. Prediction: No. 15 LSU 31, No. 9 Alabama 24 While the combination of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell provides the potential for plenty of points, this game could end up being decided by both defenses. Alabama's offensive injuries have clearly limited their ability to execute on schedule, and LSU's defense represents the best test they've faced since the loss at Tennessee. In the same manner, LSU's pass attack could set them up for some of the turnovers that have powered Alabama's excellence this season (+7 turnover margin is tied for 11th nationally) and prevent touchdowns even after successful drives. All in all, it points to a lower-scoring classic, where I'll favor the home team to make big plays late. LSU is a completely different animal in Baton Rouge. It's an afternoon game instead of an ultra-amped up night showdown in Death Valley, but it shouldn't matter too much that the Tiger fan base is just a little less … prepared. Yeah, Ole Miss, Kentucky, and Auburn are, arguably, the three best teams LSU faced, which is why those road games were tough, but LSU hasn't even let the opponents breathe at home, winning all five games by a combined score of 225-44 with the closest game a 35-6 win over Texas A&M. LSU won't destroy Alabama, and it'll be a back-and-forth fight, but there will be that moment in the second half when it all clicks, and the Tigers will put the game away with a sharp scoring drive. The crowd will take over from there. LSU 30, Alabama 23 John Brice: LSU Matt Hayes: LSU Jordan Mendoza: Alabama Paul Myerberg: LSU Erick Smith: Alabama Eddie Timanus: LSU Blake Toppmeyer: LSU Craig Meyer: Alabama 31, LSU 27 LSU 35, Alabama 28: Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt was flat out bad in his first three games: He threw three touchdowns and five interceptions against Clemson, Louisiana Tech and Ole Miss. Since then, he has completed 75.4% of his passes and has vastly reduced his turnovers as he's adjusted to coach Lane Kiffin's system. Keelon Russell can get just as hot for the Crimson Tide. We just haven't seen as much of that lately, so we'll lean toward Leavitt and Co. here. — Adam Bittner, USA TODAY This LSU team continues to impress. They now enter Week 10 ranking first in the entire country in net adjusted EPA per play, seventh in net yards per play, and seventh in net success rate. That's a step above Alabama, which ranks fifth, 15th, and ninth in those three metrics. The one weakness that LSU has is stopping the run, ranking just 54th in opponent EPA per rush, but unfortunately for the Crimson Tide, they haven't run the ball efficiently this season, ranking just 50th in EPA per rush. Without the ability to take advantage of LSU's biggest weakness, this is going to be a tough road game for Alabama. I'll lay the points with the Tigers. The sportsbooks have LSU laying nearly a touchdown at home against Alabama. That means at a neutral site, LSU would be favored by roughly a field goal, so Las Vegas believes the Tigers are the better team. While LSU has played better of late, and I would anticipate Lane Kiffin dialing up some trickeration in this game, LSU hasn't beaten Alabama since 2022 and Kiffin historically has struggled against the Tide. Give me Alabama to win a close one inside Tiger Stadium Saturday. Alabama 24, LSU 21 That last one is from The Daily Advertiser. We see what you're trying to pull, bro. There is no reason whatsoever for Alabama fans to have much confidence in this one. We have a third of the starting lineup listed as questionable, and we saw what happened in Knoxville when none of those guys played. Word is that Alabama expects to get some key players back, but will they be 100%? On top of that, Keelon Russell has struggled at times against the blitz this season, and will be facing one of the most blitz-happy teams in the country. It does appear that LSU will be without MLB Whit Weeks, so that will help. Still, this is perhaps the most hostile environment in the sport, against a team that leads the SEC in both offense and defense, that also happens to need this win to get into the playoff discussion after Tuesday night's rankings dropped. Sure, they are in this position because they lost at Ole Miss and Kentucky, but those were road games. Still, we Gump to a standard around here. The one thing that Alabama can point to is Sam Leavitt's propensity to turn the ball over, and Alabama's defense has been as opportunistic as any in the country. We're going to say that the bye week afforded Russell the opportunity to learn from film study, and Alabama will get just enough guys back to get it done in Red Stick as they have so many times in the past. Leavitt has two picks, including one returned for a touchdown, and Alabama wins 30-27. That is merely my hopium, of course. Let us know your thoughts in the comments. Matt Stahl correctly notes that Alabama needs explosive plays in the passing game to win this one. Ryan Coleman-Williams is on the road to recovery, but was still listed as questionable for LSU after missing the Tennessee and Texas A&M games. Tiger head coach Lane Kiffin predicted Thursday that the junior wideout will play, but that isn't guaranteed. Coleman-Williams can provide an explosive play threat whenever he's on the field. Against Tennessee, that lack of explosives was obvious, and contributed to the loss. That same thing can't happen in Tiger Stadium. Even if its superstar receiver can't go, Alabama has to find some big plays on offense. Lotzeir Brooks is a threat, as is Rico Scott. The Crimson Tide could also find explosives from the likes of Derek Meadows and Cederian Morgan at receiver. There always needs to be a semblance of balance, but this is not a "run the ball" game. LSU leads the SEC in rushing defense, allowing only 2.7 yards per carry and 85 yards per contest. In order to push the ball down the field, Alabama's tackles will have to neutralize DE Princewill Umanmielen. Alabama has faced some prominent pass-rushers this season, but LSU defensive end Princewill Umanmielen has a strong argument to be the best. Umanmielen's 8.5 sacks rank fifth in the country, while his 12 tackles for loss are tied for ninth. The senior is second in the SEC in each of these stat categories. There have been numerous instances this season where Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell has held the ball for too long, and giving any edge to Umanmielen, along with the rest of LSU's pass-rush — which leads the country in sacks per game (4.4) — will make it very difficult for Alabama to come out on top. None of this will be easy. That's about it for today. Have a great weekend.

away.headline: Alabama's Ryan Coleman-Williams Reportedly Expected to Return from Knee Injury vs. LSU
away.blurb: Alabama wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is expected to return for Saturday's matchup with LSU after missing the last two games with a knee injury, according to On3's Pete Nakos . The star wide receiver was out of the lineup after undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery to repair a meniscus injury. Coleman-Williams had already been playing through the injury earlier this season, but he underwent surgery after taking a hit to the head against Georgia that forced him to miss time. Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer also told The Tuscaloosa News that he's "hopeful" to see the return of offensive lineman Racin Delgatty. Defensive lineman Terrance Green is also expected to return. Both players missed Alabama's past two games with injuries as well. Coleman-Williams has 23 receptions and 415 receiving yards, both of which still rank third on the team despite his absence. The third-year wide receiver also has reeled in a team-high four receiving touchdowns and made special teams contributions on kick and punt returns. Alabama and LSU both currently hold identical 6-2 records, and the victor of their matchup could be well-positioned to earn a College Football Playoff berth. The losing team would face an uphill battle to make it to the postseason with three losses already on their schedule.

away.blurb: Wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, defensive lineman Terrance Green, and center Racin Delgatty have been cleared to return for the Crimson Tide tomorrow when Alabama takes on LSU, according to Yea Alabama . All three suffered injuries in Alabama's 20-17 loss to Georgia on October 10 and missed the Tide's 26-10 loss to Tennessee and 31-20 win over Texas A&M. Coleman-Williams, Delgatty, and Green were listed as questionable on Thursday night's availability report, alongside running backs AK Dear and EJ Crowell, offensive lineman William Sanders, and cornerback Zabien Brown. According to Pete Nakos and On3 , starting left guard William Sanders is a game-time decision for Saturday. Skip to main content Skip to site footer GET CONNECTED: TUSCALOOSA, Ala. -- The Alabama Crimson Tide was hoping to receive good news on the injury front, and fifth-ranked Alabama got it on Friday courtesy of Yea Alabama , the Crimson Tide's NIL collective. Delgatty has started every game at center for Alabama when healthy, with the Crimson Tide averaging 182.1 rushing yards in six games. Without Delgatty, the Tide averaged 61 rushing yards in two games. When Coleman-Williams left the field against Georgia, he was Alabama's leading receiver with 23 receptions for 415 yards and four touchdowns. Despite missing the last two games for the Crimson Tide, he's within 73 yards of leading the Tide in receiving. He still leads the team in receiving touchdowns, with Rico Scott in second place with three. Alabama's run defense needed Terrance Green back, with the Oregon transfer plugging the middle of the defense along the defensive line. Alabama held Georgia to 49 rushing yards in the first half when Green played. When he missed the second half, the Bulldogs had 157 yards on the ground. Tennessee had 150 yards on the ground the following week without Green in Alabama's lineup. Ace Austin is the leader of the squad, but everyone got in on the scoring action in that one. The men return to action tomorrow night against Arkansas State. Williams, Green, and Delgatty have been spotted in practice footage released this week, so there is hope for them. Lane Kiffin listed Whit Weeks as doubtful on the report but nobody is buying that. Whit has had this game circled for his return for Weeks now, pun intended. “Just all-around complete football team,” the head coach said. “You know, playing better and better football as they go. Thought the last game against Auburn was impressive. The way they came out right away, jumped on them and had a good first quarter and then obviously continued that into the third quarter too. A defensive front, actually, a defense as a whole, that just plays well together. Gets pressure on the passer and they’re at the top of the SEC and national rankings in a lot of areas, both offensively and defensively. So you know they’re a complete team.” “It feels like all of us are winning when we see Ivan out there doing what he’s doing,” McFadden said. Hopefully the recent upsets continue and I have a reason to revisit this piece after the season. But for now, we’re only looking at a score of about 33 out of 50 on the 2007 scale. Granted, that might be as close as virtually any season of the last nearly two decades has come, but if nothing else, this exercise should have reminded us just how wacky 2007 really was. If all you got out of this exercise was a reminder of Les Miles’ ridiculousness and a search of “Pat White highlights” on YouTube , it was worth it. home.headline: Alabama's Ryan Coleman-Williams Reportedly Expected to Return from Knee Injury vs. LSU
home.blurb: Alabama wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is expected to return for Saturday's matchup with LSU after missing the last two games with a knee injury, according to On3's Pete Nakos . The star wide receiver was out of the lineup after undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery to repair a meniscus injury. Coleman-Williams had already been playing through the injury earlier this season, but he underwent surgery after taking a hit to the head against Georgia that forced him to miss time. Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer also told The Tuscaloosa News that he's "hopeful" to see the return of offensive lineman Racin Delgatty. Defensive lineman Terrance Green is also expected to return. Both players missed Alabama's past two games with injuries as well. Coleman-Williams has 23 receptions and 415 receiving yards, both of which still rank third on the team despite his absence. The third-year wide receiver also has reeled in a team-high four receiving touchdowns and made special teams contributions on kick and punt returns. Alabama and LSU both currently hold identical 6-2 records, and the victor of their matchup could be well-positioned to earn a College Football Playoff berth. The losing team would face an uphill battle to make it to the postseason with three losses already on their schedule.

home.blurb: Wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, defensive lineman Terrance Green, and center Racin Delgatty have been cleared to return for the Crimson Tide tomorrow when Alabama takes on LSU, according to Yea Alabama . According to Pete Nakos and On3 , starting left guard William Sanders is a game-time decision for Saturday. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling. The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. Ohio State vs. Oregon: Need to know Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana , it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore ). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road. Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. (Ben Lonergan/The Register-Guard) 1 / 10 Oregon football vs. Northwestern updates, score, how to watch Oregon football vs. Northwestern updates, score, how to watch See photos as Oregon football hosts Northwestern at Autzen Stadium Oregon football vs. Northwestern final score, reaction to Ducks' win Dan Lanning jokes Oregon Ducks will need 12 men to stop Jeremiah Smith Oregon football ranked in initial College Football Playoff top 25 Oregon vs. Ohio State scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: Before Ohio State QB Julian Sayin went out with an injury, the Buckeyes had one of the best passing attacks in college football. Though freshman Luke Fahey has operated as the starter during Ohio State's bye week and loss to USC last week, OSU is still adjusting to life without its starting signal-caller. That's a huge advantage for an Oregon team that has settled in on its starter moving forward in Dylan Raiola and seemed to find its identity on offense in a win versus Northwestern. Why Ohio State has an advantage: No one has had an answer for Ohio State superstar and future NFL top-10 pick Jeremiah Smith. The junior has 62 catches for 1,067 yards and 13 touchdowns in eight games and is already the Big Ten's all-time leader in touchdown receptions in less than three seasons of play. Stopping Smith will be a massive challenge for the Ducks , who have shown to be susceptible against the passing game at points this season. Oregon wide receiver Dakorien Moore, left, outruns Northwestern defensive back Ore Adeyi after a catch for a touchdown as the Oregon Ducks host the Northwestern Wildcats on Oct. 31, 2026, at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon. Oregon vs. Ohio State injury updates Note: Official availability reports, mandated by the Big Ten, are released every day starting at 5 p.m. Wednesday leading up to kickoff. This story was published before the reports were made public. For Oregon: Several key Oregon contributors could return this week, though Lanning wouldn't talk about the specific status of any player during his Monday press conference and deferred to the Ducks' upcoming availability reports. Starting running back Jordon Davison was hobbled in the first half against Northwestern and was seen with crutches on the sideline in the second half, though Lanning said he didn't expect the injury to be long-term. For Ohio State: The biggest injury news for the Buckeyes revolves around Sayin, who is out for the foreseeable future since an injury versus Indiana in mid-October. Ohio State was also without standout freshman DB Jay Timmons and talented wideout Brandon Inniss vs. USC. Inniss was a game-time decision and participated in early warmups but did not play against the Trojans. Oregon outside linebacker Nasir Wyatt, left, brings down Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles as the Oregon Ducks host the Northwestern Wildcats on Oct. 31, 2026, at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon. Oregon vs. Ohio State: 4 bold predictions Oregon, Ohio State first half will be a defensive battle The Ducks rediscovered a bit of their old selves in a 38-point outing against a stout Northwestern defense last week, but the challenge will be greater this week, and the Ducks have yet to put together back-to-back good performances against good competition this season. That needs to change Saturday, but both teams, adjusting to new schemes and personnel, will get off to a slow start in Columbus this weekend. Ducks will hold Buckeyes' Jeremiah Smith under 100 yards Oregon has a good history of limiting opposing stars, though sometimes to a fault. Last season against future NFL draftee Makai Lemon and USC, the star had just 34 yards on seven catches in an Oregon win. But, that left Tanook Hines with the opportunity to cash in on the attention Lemon received. Lanning and his staff will have Smith circled everywhere, and they'll hold Smith under 100 yards, but Ohio State will still get production from other talents. Ohio State, Oregon game will come to down to field position, turnovers As most games do, Saturday's contest will come down to who commits more mistakes and who takes advantage of good field position. On the former front, Oregon has struggled mightily with protecting the ball. The Ducks have given the ball away 13 times this season, including 10 fumbles, while Ohio State has protected the ball slightly better but produces less turnovers on defense. Oregon punter Bailey Ettridge has been a massive weapon throughout the season, and if he can continually pin the Buckeyes deep, Oregon will have a good chance to spring the upset. away.headline: The hidden impact of Oregon receiver Jeremiah McClellan’s return from injury
away.blurb: COLUMBUS - The No. 23 Oregon Ducks are expected to get a valuable piece back on offense in receiver Jeremiah McClellan. McClellan has been l isted on the availability report as "probable" all week leading up to Oregon's Big Ten showdown vs. the No. 12 Ohio State Buckeyes in front of more than 100,000 expected fans at Ohio Stadium. The Crucial Timing Of Jeremiah McClellan's Return The timing is crucial for Oregon, as the Ducks have three losses but still have slim College Football Playoff chances if they win out. That path begins Saturday, Nov. 7, against the Buckeyes, who are also fighting for their playoff lives with two losses. Ducks running back Jordon Davison, receiver Messiah Hampton and tight end Andrew Olesh were all listed as out on the most recent availability report for the Ducks. "I always expect more from J-Mac. I mean, he had an unbelievable jump last year, and I think he's a guy that's become really self-aware. For you to watch him out there on the field today, and compared to when he first got here, it’s not the same guy.” This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/oregon as The Hidden Impact of Oregon Receiver Jeremiah McClellan’s Return From Injury . At Oregon Ducks on SI, we reported that McClellan was warming up last Saturday before the Ducks' win over then- No. 20 Northwestern, a solid indication of positive signs in his recovery. McClellan broke his foot while he was warming up for Portland State on Sept. 18 and has missed six games. The Oregon offense looks a lot different than when McClellan got injured. Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola is now the starter after Dante Moore suffered a concussion that is expected to be season-ending. Also, Oregon has analyst Jay Johnson calling plays after the Ducks parted ways with their offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the season. The Ducks have relied heavily on sophomore receiver Dakorien Moore, who leads the team through eight games with 41 receptions for 545 yards and six touchdowns. Moore is fresh off his best game yet, totaling a career-high 128 yards and two touchdowns on seven receptions, including a 75-yard touchdown... Oregon’s longest offensive play this season. McClellan could give Oreogn quarterback Dylan Raiola another explosive option alongside Moore. Despite playing just two games, McClellan remains tied with Moore for the team lead with two receptions of 50 yards or longer. Four of his seven catches this season gained at least 20 yards. Before his injury, McClellan led Oregon in receiving yards. Yet McClellan’s impact cannot be measured only by his receptions, receiving yards and touchdowns. In the long history of this rivalry, there's a good case that this is the biggest game ever. In his first year on the job, Will Stein has led Kentucky to a 7-1 start and a great shot at reaching the College Football Playoff with just four games remaining. His major transfer portal additions -- particularly quarterback Kenny Minchey and the offensive line -- clicked almost immediately. To this point, the Wildcats have passed all but one test they've faced, but the level of difficulty rises this weekend. Kentucky must continue to play clean football if it wants to come away with a win in Knoxville. Tennessee had two weeks to wallow in the "what if" after its three-point loss to South Carolina , but the team has to get back in the saddle this weekend. The Volunteers have the chance to pick up their second top-10 win of the season, which would really boost their CFP rankings. There's no doubt that the Vols have a playoff-caliber defense and running game, but can Josh Heupel fix the passing attack? Tennessee must improve there to reach its ceiling. Here is everything you need to know about this top-15 rivalry matchup in Knoxville. Tennessee vs. Kentucky: Need to know Rare ranked matchup: These teams have met well over 100 times, but this is just the fourth ranked matchup in history. Most recently, Tennessee and Kentucky played a top-25 matchup in 2022, with the Volunteers winning in a blowout. Prior to that, the only times the Vols and Wildcats were ranked simultaneously were in 1950 and 1951. That means there's a very good case for this matchup to be the biggest in the history of this rivalry. Games with stakes in this series usually go the way of Tennessee, but can Stein turn the tables on Saturday night? Kentucky not in the giving spirit: The holidays are approaching quickly, but Kentucky has not been feeling very generous. One of the driving factors behind the Wildcats' success is their incredible plus-13 turnover margin. That ranks first in the SEC and fourth in the entire country. For the first time since 2013, Kentucky has avoided turning the ball over in three consecutive games. If any team can end that streak, it's probably Tennessee, which has a great defense and has forced 14 turnovers in eight games. The Vols just have to protect the ball on offense. Heavy dose of DeSean Bishop : Kentucky defensive coordinator Jay Bateman probably doesn't need my advice, but I would suggest he lock in on Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop. He's been the engine of the Vols offense, and his 957 rushing yards rank sixth in the country. His 12 rushing touchdowns are tied for ninth. Over the last four games, Bishop has averaged 29 carries and 159 yards. If the Wildcats can contain Bishop and force Tennessee to throw the ball, that could be a recipe for success, but only one team has effectively shut Bishop down to this point. Kentucky's offense has been incredibly efficient, and it will pose a real challenge to the Tennessee defense. That said, the first night game in Neyland Stadium will give the Vols an edge on that side of the ball. Offensively, Tennessee leans on Bishop and gets enough out of its passing game to pull away from Kentucky late and cover the one-score spread. The Tennessee Vols are currently on the outside looking in at the 12-team College Football Playoff. Tennessee, which is 6-2 with four games remaining, was ranked No. 13 in the initial CFP rankings. The shocking part of Tennessee's ranking isn't that they were at No. 13 — we expected them to be in that range — it's that they were somehow ranked eight spots behind a two-loss Alabama team that lost by 16 points to the Vols a couple of weeks ago. Nearly everyone in college football media was shocked to see Alabama ranked that many spots ahead of the Vols. "Tennessee just whooped Alabama," said former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray after the rankings were revealed. "I mean, they whooped Alabama. And you're going to tell me that Alabama is at No. 5 and Tennessee's at No. 13 in this ranking? I do not like Alabama at No. 5" The good news for the Vols is that they still control their own destiny. If Tennessee wins out in November, they'll secure a spot in the 12-team playoff. And that November journey begins this Saturday with a huge game against Kentucky in Neyland Stadium. Kentucky is ranked No. 6 in the initial College Football Playoff rankings. Murray, who called Tennessee's game against Arkansas for ESPN earlier this season, has the Vols beating the Wildcats 31-21 on Saturday. "I think George MacIntyre continues to mature in the offense," said Murray. "I have been really impressed with his growth as the starting quarterback over the past month, and he's got some really good receivers. Mike Matthews is electric with the football. They find creative ways to get him on skinny slants and quick screens to the outside. And I like the way they use DaSaahn Brame, the tight end. … He's very athletic and very fast, which is why him against (Kentucky linebacker) Grant Godfrey is gonna be very interesting in the pass game because both of those guys are long and can move. "But at the end of the day, I will continue to doubt Kentucky. I'm gonna do it myself again. I just had Kentucky, too, and I said I would stop doing it. But I like Tennessee. I like Tennessee a lot. I think Tennessee wins 31-21." Kentucky and Tennessee will kick off at 6:15 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ESPN. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. "We have a, you know, awesome opportunity this week to play an elite SEC opponent in Tennessee on the road. You know, I think they're playing extremely well as a team. Neyland broke the college football decibel record in Tennessee's Oct. 17 win over the Alabama Crimson Tide, who committed six pre-snap penalties in a 26-10 loss. picks.blurb: Tennessee offense preview: Can Kentucky force the Vols to pass? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Story by Wildcats Wire Tennessee offense preview: Can Kentucky force the Vols to pass? Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Wed, November 4, 2026 at 2:31 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to Knoxville to face off against the #16 Tennessee Volunteers on Saturday night, and both teams are coming off of a bye week. We previewed the Tennessee defense and the big scheme showdown between Will Stein's offense against Jim Knowles' defense. Now we will take a look at the Tennessee offense that has consistently put up points under head coach Josh Heupel. Heupel's offense this year has struggled in some areas, and it has resembled the 2024 offense in a lot of ways. Since becoming the head coach of Tennessee in 2021, Josh Heupel has had his offense scoring a lot of points and he is 5-0 against Kentucky . Mark Stoops and Brad White could not figure out Heupel's up-tempo offense that features extremely wide splits from the wide receivers that creates a light box to run the football. Heupel's offenses are averaging over 40 points per game in this series. It is time to see if the new scheme change that has taken place under Jay Bateman will be more effective in slowing down this scheme. This scheme is creative because the wide splits create light boxes that the Vols will then use their ground game to run into favorable looks. Once Tennessee gets the run game going, they will then take shots down the field on deep option routes. However, this offense is similar to the 2024 version, which has become heavily dependent on the run game getting going. The quarterback situation is in the worst position it has been in under Heupel. Heupel is playing the cards close to his chest and continuing to use gamesmanship by not naming a starter. True freshman Faizon Brandon started the season and after struggling then getting a minor injury, the Vols switched to redshirt freshman George MacIntyre and have not switched back since. MacIntyre has ran the offense better in my opinion, he is less frantic in the pocket and is better at getting the ball out of his hands. The only issue is MacIntyre has not pushed the football down the field much, his 5.7 average depth of target is the lowest in the SEC and is obviously a critical element of Heupel's scheme. MacIntyre will get the start, but I wouldn't be surprised to see a little bit of Faizon Brandon as well to try and throw off Kentucky's defense. Kentucky has faced a dual threat quarterback every week of the season to this point, I am intrigued to see how this pass rush gets after a quarterback that is a pocket passer like MacIntyre. It is something we have yet to see, and this is an area that could be a massive advantage for the Wildcats. It is important that Kentucky wins the early downs on defense and force Tennessee to beat them through the air. Tennessee's offense is led by running back DeSean Bishop, and the Vols will absolutely try to feed him in this football game. Tennessee ranks third in the SEC in yards per rush and EPA per rush, they are very much a run heavy offense. Tennessee is still getting explosive plays in this offense, they have a 12.6 explosive play rate which is third in the conference. The Vols rank second in the SEC with a 15.3 explosive run rate and they rank 13th with a 9.6 explosive pass rate. Tennessee ranks 13th in the SEC in EPA per dropback and yards per pass attempt. They rank 11th in the conference with a 42.5% pass success rate. This is simple for Kentucky, stack the box and slow down this run game. Kentucky has to sell out to stop the run and force the Vols to beat them with their quarterbacks, whether it be MacIntyre or Brandon. DeSean Bishop is one of the best running backs in the country, he has 957 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the season. Bishop is averaging over 100 yards per game and 5.6 yards per carry. He helps the Vols convert on early downs, as their 46.5% early down conversion rate ranks sixth in the SEC. However, they have struggled to convert on third down like Kentucky as they have converted just 35.5% of third down opportunities this season, which ranks 15th in the SEC. In our self scout over the bye week, we pointed out how Kentucky's run defense really improved in the month of October. This has to continue for Kentucky to win this football game, but it will be easier said than done. Jay Bateman has to force Tennessee into a dropback heavy game by getting his defense to stop the run. If they can successfully do that, they will be in a great position to win this game. picks.headline: Tennessee vs Kentucky predictions: Can Vols derail Wildcats’ SEC title hopes?
picks.blurb: November kicks up the stakes in college football, especially with the release of the first College Football Playoff rankings this past Tuesday. And one of Saturday's key games features unlikely SEC contender Kentucky (No. 7 in the US LBM Coaches Poll ) visiting Neyland Stadium to face No. 16 Tennessee . Kentucky landed at No. 6 in the first CFP rankings, while the Vols landed at No. 13, controversially eight spots lower than Alabama — a team it beat by 16 points. Kentucky controls its path to a place it has never been: the SEC championship game. The Wildcats are tied with Georgia atop the conference at 5-1, and winning their final three SEC games would send them to Atlanta. But that run starts with a major obstacle Saturday at Tennessee, where Kentucky has won just 11 times and lost five straight in the rivalry. Florida and Missouri follow, while Georgia faces its own three-game test. First-year Wildcats coach Will Stein isn’t hiding from the stakes, but he knows Kentucky’s historic opportunity disappears quickly if the Wildcats look ahead: “If you don't handle your business this week? Then nothing really matters.” Watch Vols vs Wildcats live on Fubo Tennessee likely needs a 10-2 record to make the playoff. There’s also a chance that 9-3 could be good enough, but that possibility also would require a win over Kentucky. So who wins on Saturday? Here's what you need to know for one of Week 10's marquee games, including predictions from USA TODAY Sports reporters and beat writers from the Knoxville News Sentinel and Louisville Courier Journal , part of the USA TODAY Network. Who will start at QB for Tennessee vs Kentucky: George MacIntyre or Faizon Brandon? Tennessee football coach Josh Heupel still won’t publicly name George MacIntyre his starting quarterback. His players seem to have done it for him . Teammates say the sophomore has “taken control of the offense” and emerged as its leader since replacing Faizon Brandon against Auburn. With the Vols 3-1 in MacIntyre’s starts and still chasing a College Football Playoff berth, the quarterback question appears increasingly settled as Tennessee prepares for a top-20 showdown with Kentucky. Can Jim Knowles slow Will Stein's Kentucky offense? Will Stein knows exactly how dangerous Jim Knowles can be. Kentucky’s coach has matched wits with Tennessee’s defensive coordinator three times over the past two seasons, producing dramatic games, tactical counterpunches and lessons that could shape their Nov. 7 reunion. Knowles has never forced a turnover against a Stein offense, but he dominated their biggest matchup. On Saturday, Marcus Freeman could do the same against the same program. No. 11 Notre Dame and No. 1 Miami meet in South Bend with playoff implications on the line in what is the highest-ranked matchup between the programs (according to the AP poll) since that classic Catholics vs. Convicts showdown in 1988. The Irish won the national championship that season, its most recent title. The College Football Playoff selection committee sees a different matchup. Miami sits atop the first CFP rankings, but slotted Notre Dame at No. 11, seven spots lower than the AP voters. Notre Dame is the last team in the CFP field, and a loss against Miami could knock the Irish out of playoff contention entirely. "They don't have that signature win right now," CFP committee chair Hunter Yurachek said Tuesday night on ESPN. "They've got a great opportunity in front of them at home versus Miami to get that signature win that I think they need to move up in the rankings." Don't forget, we've been here before. Miami defeated Notre Dame 27-24 in last season's season opener. The Irish remained above Miami in five CFP rankings, but the committee flipped the two in the final week, placing Miami over Notre Dame in the CFP. Miami vs. Notre Dame: Need to know Darian Mensah vs. a defense without its leader : Darian Mensah leads the FBS in completion percentage (80.7%) and pass efficiency (202.7) and is tied for the national lead with 25 touchdown passes against one interception. Notre Dame takes him on without linebacker Drayk Bowen , its leading tackler (45) and the green-dot helmet that relays defensive calls. He was ruled out with an ankle injury suffered against Navy . Malachi Toney's absence : Miami will be without superstar receiver Malachi Toney, who suffered an ankle injury in practice Wednesday and will undergo surgery in hopes of returning for the CFP. This game certainly takes on a different context. The sophomore ranks in the top three nationally in receptions (73), receiving yards per game (128.4) and receiving touchdowns (13), the last of which ties Miami's single-season school record. Cooper Barkate is the second-best receiver on the roster, but he averages 46.5 yards per game, compared to Toney's 128.4. CJ Carr's problem : Carr has been magnificent most of his career, but the splits are wild. He's thrown 18 touchdowns and one interception this season, and he is 15-0 as a starter against unranked teams. Against AP-ranked opponents, he is 2-3, completing 60.9% of his passes at 6.6 yards per attempt with six touchdowns and five interceptions. With few opportunities to impress the CFP committee, he needs to step up against the top-ranked Hurricanes. Unranked Boston College , SMU and Syracuse are the only teams remaining on the schedule. Notre Dame's invincibility : Notre Dame is 10-1 at home against Miami, and the home team has won the last eight on-campus meetings. Miami's only win at Notre Dame Stadium came in 1984. On the other side, the Hurricanes are 18-3 on the road as the AP No. 1, with all three losses at ranked teams, including the 1988 game against the Irish. Miami hasn't defeated an AP top-5 team on the road since 2005. Penalties and the red zone : Notre Dame is the most disciplined team in the FBS, averaging only 28.9 penalty yards per game. Miami ranks 82nd (58.8). The Irish defense, however, ranks 108th in red-zone defense, allowing points on 88.9% of possessions, and Miami scores on 92.9% of its own. History sides with the Irish. Now that Malachi Toney is out, siding with the Irish becomes an easy play. Notre Dame will play the nation's most efficient quarterback either way, but how different does he look without his top option? Meanwhile, Notre Dame's red-zone defense has struggled against far lesser offenses, so will Toney's absence actually matter? Miami is 5-3 against the spread this season. Notre Dame is 4-4. The Irish can win this game, but covering by five points will still be difficult. picks.blurb: Rece Davis Predicts Notre Dame Playoff Problem Ahead of Top-5 Miami Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Notre Dame could find itself in the same College Football Playoff predicament that ended its 2025 season if it can’t beat No. 1 Miami on Saturday, according to ESPN College GameDay host Rece Davis. Davis made the case on ESPN’s College GameDay Podcast with co-hosts Pete Thamel and Dan Wetzel, saying the No. 4 Fighting Irish (7-1) would be in “ very much the same situation as a year ago ” with a loss. Rece Davis on Notre Dame’s resume Notre Dame Fighting Irish head coach Marcus Freeman reacts during the first half against the Brigham Young Cougars | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis said that split will shape the debate over the Irish. He expects them to stay in the field unless the Hurricanes blow them out, but he doesn’t see the questions about their resume going away. “I think Notre Dame will still be OK absent getting run out of the stadium, which I cannot conceive of happening,” Davis said. “So it’s going to be a little bit different than last year, but the argument, the discussion, is going to be the same if they don’t win this game.” He added: “When you get down to who did you play and who did you beat, especially the who did you beat portion of who did you play, they won’t have much on the paper.” Why does Notre Dame’s schedule matter? General view as Brigham Young Cougars fans celebrate on the field after the game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. The Irish beat Wisconsin, Rice, Michigan State, Purdue, North Carolina, Stanford and Navy. After Miami, they close with Boston College, SMU and Syracuse, who are a combined 14-10 and unranked. Notre Dame does carry a protection it lacked last year. The College Football Playoff guarantees the Irish a spot if they finish in the top 12 of the final rankings. A loss to Miami would test that cushion, though, because Notre Dame would sit at 7-2 with no win over a ranked opponent and no ranked teams left on its schedule. Miami vs. Notre Dame stakes Miami Hurricanes head coach Mario Cristobal celebrates after defeating the Florida State Seminoles | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last season, Miami and Notre Dame both finished 10-2, and the selection committee used the Hurricanes’ 27-24 win in Week 1 to award them the final at-large spot. The Irish were the first team out and declined a bowl invitation. Last season, Miami and Notre Dame both finished 10-2, and the selection committee used the Hurricanes’ 27-24 win in Week 1 to award them the final at-large spot. The Irish were the first team out and declined a bowl invitation. Notre Dame athletic director Pete Bevacqua said at the time, “ We feel like the playoff was stolen from our student-athletes.” Davis called the rematch “another little delicious subplot” and said Notre Dame’s frustration “wasn’t necessarily just directed at Miami.” Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman made “ leave no doubt ” the program’s mantra for 2026 after the snub. Saturday gives the Irish that chance against an 8-0 Miami team that leads FBS at 47.6 points per game, while Notre Dame’s defense leads FBS at 236.1 yards allowed per game. The committee releases its first College Football Playoff rankings of the season Tuesday at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN, and Miami vs. Notre Dame kicks off Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. picks.blurb: Miami Hurricanes Get Surprise Odds For Matchup Against Notre Dame - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Miami Hurricanes Get Surprise Odds For Matchup Against Notre Dame (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Shandel Richardson · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 1, 2026 at 5:02 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Miami Hurricanes are the No. 1 team in college football in the eyes of the voters. When it comes to the gambling websites, however, it's a bit different. The odds were released for Saturday's game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in South Bend, Ind. According to Hard Rock Bet, the Hurricanes are a 4.5 underdog in the matchup. This should come as a surprise and it shouldn't. Despite the top ranking, the Hurricanes have shown some flaws this season. Their play on defense has been one of the issues. On Saturday, they gave up 407 yards in the 38-35 victory against the North Carolina Tar Heels. They were assisted by a late fumble recovery and the Tar Heels being twice called for a penalty on two onside kicks to avoid the upset. Despite their dominance on offense, the Hurricanes have given up at least 20 points in three games. They struggled in a 33-20 victory against the Wake Forest Demon Deacons in September. They then needed two overtimes to defeat the Florida State Seminoles in a 45-43 shootout. The Seminoles, who were a failed Hail Mary attempt from stealing a victory, amassed 433 yards. Even though the Hurricanes defeated the Pittsburgh Panthers by 29 points, they still allowed 403 yards. At some point, they need to show they can at least come up with stops should the high-powered offense have an off night. The offense, led by quarterback Darian Mensah, receiver Malachi Toney and running back Mark Fletcher, has carried UM all season. Mensah and Toney are both Heisman candidates while Fletcher just set the school record for most career touchdowns with 38. That is saying a lot considering the amount of talent that has come through Coral Gables over the years. Even though they are favored, the Fighting Irish have struggled the last two games. They had difficulty early on against the Navy Midshipmen before pulling away for a 35-13 victory on Saturday. Two weeks before, Notre Dame was upset by the BYU Cougars of the Big 12 conference. That loss now looks even worse after the Cougars followed that win with a bad loss to the UCF Knights, who were blown out Friday by the Baylor Bears. Regardless, it doesn't matter who is favored in the Miami-Notre Dame game. It is the biggest matchup of the weekend. ESPN has already dubbed it as the home for the popular College Gameday show.

away.headline: Malachi Toney's injury, explained: Doctor outlines Miami WR's return timeline and 2026 outlook
away.blurb: Per the school, Toney will undergo surgery to repair the sprain, which will put him out for at least the remainder of Miami's regular season. home.headline: Why Bill O’Brien Hopes Boston College Captain Michael Crounse Returns Against Notre Dame
home.blurb: CHESTNUT HILL, Mass. — The morning after Boston College football’s initial student-athlete availability report for Saturday’s contest against FSU came out, head coach Bill O’Brien spoke on the injury designation for Michael Crounse, the Eagles’ starting center and a prized team captain. The impact Crounse has for BC is paramount for a variety of reasons — that could be seen when he made his return from injury against Georgia Tech in Week 8 , as the Eagles ran for nearly 400 yards. But in BC’s Week 9 loss on the road to Duke , his lower leg got rolled on quite badly in the second half, which forced him out of the game and into a boot. “I mean, he’s progressing,” said O’Brien. “He was in a boot. He’s out of the boot already. So we’ll see for Notre Dame. [I] really, really want him to play against Notre Dame.” While Crounse is officially out this week, the Eagles’ road contest in South Bend, Ind., next week against the Fighting Irish will be a particularly special one for the redshirt junior. Boston College Football Tight End Kaelan Chudzinski Confirmed Available for Duke Game But the main reason that he makes such a big difference on the field stems from his veteran presence in the huddle, which is undeniably a key trait in all levels of sport, especially football. After suffering a knee injury in the Eagles’ Week 1 loss at Cincinnati, Crounse missed four straight games before returning against the Yellow Jackets, and he finished that game without any major setbacks. O’Brien technically confirmed it isn’t a season-ending injury, which is positive news for the Eagles. But it will at least sideline him for this week’s matchup, and possibly one that has been marked on Crounse’s calendar for months. That is because Crounse’s father, Mike, played for Notre Dame from 1986-90, highlighted by a consensus national championship in an undefeated 12-0 1988 season. “It’s a special game for him,” O’Brien said. “But there’s not much we can do about it. We feel terrible for Mike, but it is what it is.” Freshman DJ Williams, who has a 48.7 offensive grade on PFF (Pro Football Focus), which ranks near the very bottom of FBS centers that qualify for a grade, will be making his fifth-career start in Crounse’s place. It is not an ideal situation to be thrust into as an underclassmen, especially as a replacement for a captain of all people. But Williams now has enough experience under his belt to enter Saturday’s showdown with the Seminoles carrying a bit more confidence than he had at the beginning of the season, when he was essentially tossed straight into the ring of fire with no legitimate playing time to lean on as a guidance tool. “DJ’s got another opportunity,” O’Brien said. “And DJ’s had a good week. The Bulldogs came back from a nine-point fourth-quarter deficit in the first meeting, outscoring the Rebels 17-0 in the fourth to win 43-35, but Ole Miss would have its revenge. It was in the College Football Playoff quarterfinal at the Sugar Bowl that the Rebels ended Georgia's season with a 39-34 win thanks largely to the heroics of quarterback Trinidad Chambliss . So what will these two deliver this year? While plenty has changed from last year's teams to this year, both quarterbacks return, and there are high stakes involved here. Georgia debuted at No. 2 in the first College Football Playoff rankings of the season, and a win here would solidify their chances of reaching the SEC Championship. On the other side, the Rebels need a win to gain firmer ground. They're No. 10 in the rankings, putting them on the precipice of losing an at-large bid. Plus, a loss here would be their third in SEC play, essentially ending their conference title hopes, and putting them in a position where they need to win out and hope for some other teams to lose to return to the playoff. Georgia vs. Ole Miss: Need to know This is the fifth straight time these two have met while ranked: Maybe that doesn't seem like something that's all that impressive to you, but for context, it had happened only five times in the first 46 meetings between the schools. Georgia has had the better end of most meetings, as they lead the series 34-14-1, and a win for Ole Miss this weekend would give the Rebels consecutive wins over the Dawgs for the first time since the 1995 and 1996 seasons. Kirby Smart has done well against ranked opponents: The Georgia coach is 44-18 against AP-ranked teams during his tenure in Athens. picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football vs. Ole Miss Football on Saturday Night Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Georgia Bulldogs and the Ole Miss Rebels will face off on Saturday night in Oxford, Mississippi in one of college football's most anticipated matchups. These two teams played twice last year. One game was in Athens and one was in the Sugar Bowl for a College Football Playoff quarterfinal game. Both were epic showdowns that involved second half comebacks. So that means that Kirby Smart and Pete Golding could be in for another back and forth game. These two teams feature some of the best players in the entire county. Georgia is favored, and advanced stats point this in Georgia’s favor, but Ole Miss has Trinidad Chambliss and the home crowd. Let’s make three bold predictions: Georgia Sacks Trinidad Chambliss at Least Three Times This is a different Georgia defense that Chambliss will be facing off against. Last year, the Dawgs managed just 20 sacks in 14 games. They are up to 26 this season in only eight games. Georgia didn’t take Chambliss down behind the line of scrimmage a single time in either matchup a season ago. Part of that was because of the magician-like escapability Chambliss showed off in new Orleans. This year is different for this defense and Chris Cole has leveled up to be one of the biggest difference makers on that side of the ball in all of college football. Georgia has gotten to the quarterback in big games this year, and Chambliss’ pocket presence and athleticism makes three sacks a bold prediction. Dawgs Clear 200 Yards on the Ground, Again Georgia is averaging 200 yards per game on the ground. They hit that number on the road against Alabama. They hit that number last week against the Florida Gators. Ole Miss has shown that you can run all over them if you get a lead. Florida bullied the Rebels down in Gainesville, totalling 302 yards on the ground. That was when Florida was a lot more explosive on offense, but still, Ole Miss showed it was possible. Georgia is clearly a run-first offense, and Nate Frazier looked a lot closer to the Nate Frazier we saw at the beginning of the season in Georgia’s win last week. His health would bring a huge boost to the run game, making the explosive Dwight Phillips Jr. a complimentary weapon and a change of pace back. Chambliss Gets Picked Twice The only SEC games where Georgia wasn’t forcing turnovers were against Auburn and Vanderbilt. Even then, they did get an interception against the Commodores. Georgia’s defense has been a lot more opportunistic this season. A handful of different players have forced fumbles. Eliis Robinson IV is shaping up to be a first-round pick. Demello Jones is forcing turnovers. Even Braylon Conley got an interception last week. Chambliss has thrown eight interceptions already this season. He only threw three all last year. He is being asked to do more because Ole Miss is not running the football as well, and Ole Miss is getting into deficits. Georgia’s defense is the best they will face all year. Even if Ole Miss wins or it is close, two interceptions is completely possible against a vaunted Dawgs defense. The reigning SEC champion Bulldogs have one loss, but the Rebels have two and can't afford a third. What happens here will have a major effect on the shape of the College Football Playoff. Here are five trends we expect will determine who walks off the field a winner. 1. Ole Miss puts the game in Trinidad Chambliss' hands Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss has been one of the SEC's most productive offensive players, leading the conference with 2,189 passing yards and 18 touchdowns. He's also added seven rushing touchdowns. Georgia's defense allows just 14.9 points per game, ranking top 15 nationally. Expect Georgia's pass rush and secondary to credibly test Chambliss' long-range passing ambitions. His ability to extend plays and create offense with his legs could be critical. 2.
