Ole Miss is one of the SEC's worst run defenses, allowing 148.9 yards on average. The Bulldogs have several capable running backs, including Dwight Phillips Jr. and Bo Walker, particularly with injuries affecting the running back rotation. If Georgia controls the line of scrimmage, it can dictate tempo, keep Chambliss on the sideline and make life difficult for the Ole Miss defense. More: Bold predictions for college football's biggest Week 10 games 3. Kewan Lacy's absence hurts Ole Miss Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy is unlikely to play because of a shoulder injury, according to head coach Pete Golding. That puts additional pressure on Makhi Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight to provide production. Georgia ranks second nationally in rushing defense, allowing just 86 yards per game. Without Lacy, establishing a consistent running game becomes an even bigger challenge. 4. Expect Georgia to attack early Georgia has outscored opponents 94-14 in first quarters this season. The Bulldogs have also scored 41 points per game, ranking first in the SEC. Quarterback Gunner Stockton has completed 71.8 percent of his passes. Ole Miss needs to avoid an early deficit. Georgia's ability to build leads could force the Rebels into a more predictable, pass-heavy offensive approach. 5. Ole Miss' home-field advantage matters Oct 31, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) looks on during the fourth quarter against the Auburn Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images The Rebels have won 16 consecutive games at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, the longest active home winning streak among Power Four programs. With the crowd behind them and a quarterback capable of creating explosive plays, Ole Miss has reasons to believe it can make this a difficult night for Georgia. The Bottom Line Georgia needs to establish its rushing attack, pressure Chambliss, and take advantage of its defensive superiority. Ole Miss needs explosive quarterback play, improved rushing production, and an early lead to build on. The biggest question: Can Ole Miss' offense generate enough against one of the nation's top-scoring defenses, particularly without its leading running back? away.blurb: Georgia Finally Seeing Highly Anticipated Return of Transfer WR This Week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Georgia Finally Seeing Highly Anticipated Return of Transfer WR This Week It's not going to be an easy one as the Rebels have certainly had Georgia's numbers over the last couple of years and Trinidad Chambliss has had some huge games against the Dawgs. With that being said, Georgia at its best offensively should be able to score enough to win this game. Unfortunately, the Dawgs have not been at that best over the last couple of games, but it sounds like they are set to see the return of a weapon they though at the beginning of the season could be their top wide receiver. On the initial Wednesday night availability report, Canion was listed as probable, but by Thursday night, he was removed entirely and now looks set to make his return to the wide receiver core this week. Isiah Canion transferred in somewhat controversially from hated rival Georgia Tech after a productive year for the Yellow Jackets, and after getting off to a slow start, he suffered a leg injury in the middle of September and has not been seen from since. This week though, he returns and could be a significant X-factor for this offense. It would not be a surprise to see the Dawgs ease him in slowly, especially since he was not super involved in the passing game before he was injured. With that being said, Canion was expected to be the kind of difference maker who could take things to the next level on the outside, so there could be an urgency to get him involved. To this point, Canion has not been able to live up to the billing from when he came in as a transfer, but a big play in this game would change everything in terms of how fans view him. Keep an eye on the big bodied wide receiver this week and in the weeks ahead to make an impact on this passing game.

away.headline: Terez Davis off Ole Miss injury report as Rebels prepare for Georgia
away.blurb: There weren’t many changes to the Student-Athlete Availability Report for Georgia and Ole Miss on Thursday night. The most noteworthy update was Ole Miss starting left tackle Terez Davis being removed entirely from the report . His availability for Saturday against No. 2 Georgia was never in real doubt, but we’ve seen in recent weeks players land on the report and not able to play a full game that following Saturday. Having Davis off the report means the Rebels will have its entire starting offensive line available to face a Bulldogs defense that has recorded 26 sacks this season already. And Ole Miss is going to need every bit of protection it can get. Georgia is allowing just 14.9 points and 273.4 total yards per game, ranking among the nation's best defenses in both categories. The Bulldogs have been particularly difficult to run against, surrendering just 86.8 rushing yards per game. Linebackers Chris Cole and Raylen Wilson have been especially disruptive, combining for 16.5 tackles for loss and 7.5 sacks. They're a big reason opposing offenses have struggled to consistently move the football against Georgia. That's what makes having Davis available so important. The Rebels have done an excellent job protecting quarterback Trinidad Chambliss this season, allowing just one sack over their last three games. Even when Davis missed the Texas game, Ole Miss managed to keep Chambliss upright. But Georgia presents a different challenge. With Kewan Lacy already ruled out, the Rebels will need their offensive line to create running lanes for Shekai Mills-Knight and the other running backs while also giving Chambliss enough time to find open receivers. Davis' return to the lineup against Auburn was encouraging. Having him completely off the injury report heading into one of the biggest games of the season is even better news. home.headline: Terez Davis off Ole Miss injury report as Rebels prepare for Georgia
home.blurb: There weren’t many changes to the Student-Athlete Availability Report for Georgia and Ole Miss on Thursday night. The most noteworthy update was Ole Miss starting left tackle Terez Davis being removed entirely from the report . His availability for Saturday against No. 2 Georgia was never in real doubt, but we’ve seen in recent weeks players land on the report and not able to play a full game that following Saturday. Having Davis off the report means the Rebels will have its entire starting offensive line available to face a Bulldogs defense that has recorded 26 sacks this season already. And Ole Miss is going to need every bit of protection it can get. Georgia is allowing just 14.9 points and 273.4 total yards per game, ranking among the nation's best defenses in both categories. The Bulldogs have been particularly difficult to run against, surrendering just 86.8 rushing yards per game. Linebackers Chris Cole and Raylen Wilson have been especially disruptive, combining for 16.5 tackles for loss and 7.5 sacks. They're a big reason opposing offenses have struggled to consistently move the football against Georgia. That's what makes having Davis available so important. The Rebels have done an excellent job protecting quarterback Trinidad Chambliss this season, allowing just one sack over their last three games. Even when Davis missed the Texas game, Ole Miss managed to keep Chambliss upright. But Georgia presents a different challenge. With Kewan Lacy already ruled out, the Rebels will need their offensive line to create running lanes for Shekai Mills-Knight and the other running backs while also giving Chambliss enough time to find open receivers. Davis' return to the lineup against Auburn was encouraging. Having him completely off the injury report heading into one of the biggest games of the season is even better news. home.blurb: Thursday Ole Miss vs. Georgia Injury Report: Terez Davis Cleared, Franklin Questionable Recent ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – The SEC's Thursday availability report for Georgia week is out, and No. 10 Ole Miss left tackle Terez Davis is no longer listed after being probable Wednesday. Defensive end Kam Franklin and linebacker Keaton Thomas remain questionable for Saturday night. Franklin and Thomas were questionable on Wednesday's report as well, so their status has not changed. Davis and cornerback Cedrick Beavers were both probable Wednesday and are no longer listed, while cornerback Jalyn Crawford and safety MJ Preston remain probable. Running back Kewan Lacy is out again. The report was posted at 7:10 p.m. CT on Thursday. Davis, a left tackle, was probable on Wednesday and does not appear on Thursday's report, which means he has no availability designation heading into the weekend. Cornerback Cedrick Beavers was also probable Wednesday and is no longer listed. Crawford and Preston stay probable. Keaton Thomas and Kam Franklin remain questionable Thomas and Franklin carry the same questionable tag they had on Wednesday, so Ole Miss has not cleared either defender with Saturday night's kickoff about two days away. Linebacker Luke Ferrelli, who has been dealing with an ankle injury, is not listed on the report for the second straight day. Kewan Lacy is out again as he works back from the shoulder injury he suffered at Texas, and the same nine Rebels are out as Wednesday. Franklin is listed as questionable on Thursday's report, the same as Wednesday. Updated statuses are expected on the SEC's pregame availability report before kickoff. Georgia's report is nearly the same as Wednesday's. Outside linebacker Amaris Williams is out, and receiver Thomas Blackshear, running back Chauncey Bowens, tight end Elyiss Williams, inside linebacker AJ Kruah, safety Tyriq Green and defensive lineman Joseph Jonah-Ajonye are questionable. Receiver Isiah Canion, who was probable Wednesday, is no longer listed. picks.headline: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida?
picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? Oklahoma Sooners tight ends coach Jason Witten will take over as interim offensive coordinator for the rest of the season. | Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Gators have an impressive resume, having beaten No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28 at The Swamp, then going on the road to Austin and taking down No. 7 Texas 27-24 - one week after OU beat them in Dallas - on a night the underwhelming Florida defense overwhelmed Arch Manning and the Longhorns, sacking him five times, limiting UT to 2-of-10 on third down (they had 13 first downs total) and holding the Horns to 272 total yards. But they were also blown out in back-to-back losses to No. 25 Missouri and unranked South Carolina, which preceded last week's 27-8 loss to No. 3 Georgia. Oklahoma is a touchdown underdog to Florida, but the Sooners are the best defense the Gators face. Still, OU may be reeling after its worst defensive performance in years in the blowout loss to South Carolina - which included an incomprehensible 25 missed tackles (usually 10 is a bad number). OU's first trip to The Swamp will be punctuated by another big game from Gators RB Jaden Baugh, who's third in the SEC at 100.3 rushing yards per game and first with 13 rushing TDs. Final score: Florida 28, Oklahoma 21 Things could get gross Saturday night. Florida has officially made a quarterback change, and Tramell Jones Jr. could be without a pair of key weapons to pair with an already banged up offensive line. Oklahoma's offense has been so bad it got its coordinator fired, but Jason Witten has never called plays collegiately and John Mateer is still likely the quarterback the Sooners will roll with. OU's defense needs to bounce back after its tackling struggles last week, but even an improved showing could see Gator running back Jaden Baugh have enough success to push Jon Sumrall's team across the finish line. Final: Florida 16, Oklahoma 13 OU is set up for further disaster as it heads to the swamp. Jason Witten will serve as the Sooners' play caller for the first time at the college level, John Mateer is still the quarterback and Ben Hill Griffin Stadium is one of the nation's most hostile atmospheres. But amid the weirdness, I expect OU to win this game. Teams often come out more inspired after a notable firing, and I predict Witten will lead a creative game plan as he auditions for the full-time offensive coordinator role. Florida's offense is good - but it is also prone to turning the ball over. If the Sooners are able to put pressure on Tramell Jones Jr. early, it will create a long day for the Gators' offense. Final: Oklahoma 24, Florida 20 The Sooners figure to get a little boost from Jason Witten's playcalling, but don't expect massive changes in either scheme or production here. The offensive line still has its issues, John Mateer hasn't been consistent at all, and neither of the other quarterbacks have experience in games like this. But Oklahoma's defense does figure to have a bounce-back game after struggling to contain LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina offense. The tackling will be better, and Florida's offense is in a bit of flux itself with Tramell Jones Jr. expected to make his second start of the season at quarterback and Florida's offensive line struggling in recent weeks. But the Gators still have plenty of talent, especially on the offensive side, and The Swamp is one of the toughest environments in college football. That's a tough position for a reeling team to be placed in. The game will be close into the second half but the Gators figure to pull away and hand Oklahoma its second consecutive defeat. Final: Florida 24, Oklahoma 14 Brady Trantham A new offensive coordinator doesn'tchange the fact that John Mateer is still QB1 at OU. Mateer gives Oklahoma their best shot in any game, but in 20 games as the Sooner signal caller, it is apparent that he simply isn't very good. A coaching change can, in theory, help him in spots, but if OU needs their QB to make a play in a tight game, chances are he will make that play - just for the other team. Florida sticks to the run and gets Oklahoma on a few explosives and rides it to an easy win. The Sooners need to win two of their final four to earn bowl eligibility . With a new voice leading the offense, the Sooners are hoping for a turnaround to end the 2026 season. Jason Witten takes over an offense that has underachieved this season, given the number of returning starters along the offensive line and the weapons at returning quarterback John Mateer. How much better can Oklahoma be in a week is the question on everyone's minds. It's unlikely the Sooners will suddenly erupt on offense, but if they find more consistency, they'll have a chance to finish the season on a high note. So how will the Sooners perform in "The Swamp?" Our staff here at Sooners Wire picked this week's showdown between the Sooners and the Gators. Too Many Questions Oklahoma tight ends coach Jason Witten, left, talks with coach Brent Venables during a Sooners football spring practice in Norman, Okla., Thursday, April 9, 2026. There are just too many moving parts for Oklahoma to reliably believe the Sooners could win a road game in the swamp. The Sooners have made a change at offensive coordinator and the availability of a bunch of notable players on both sides of the ball are still in question. There's also the question of how Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer will play without Ben Arbuckle on the sideline for the first time in years. Even though Florida has a few issues to worry about as well, they're certainly not as dire as Oklahoma's at the moment. Florida 21, Oklahoma 10 James D. Witten called plays as a high school head coach and had a ton of success doing it. I think the offense will play with a fire we haven't seen this year, and the defense will return to its dominant ways. Because of that, I've got OU winning and the offense scoring three touchdowns. The Sooners' offense totaled just 118 yards and three points through three quarters as they fell to the Gamecocks , 42-25. "Incredibly pissed at myself and for all of us," Venables said. "Just embarrassing. It's embarrassing in every way." Loud boos rang throughout Gaylord Family — Oklahoma Memorial Stadium during the game and the student section chanted "fire Arbuckle," referring to offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle . It's not out of the realm of possibility that Venables elects to make a change at playcaller. Venables said postgame he still believes the offense is fixable but what that looks like moving forward is unclear. While the biggest questions surrounding the program are the future at offensive coordinator, quarterback and getting the program back to contention, there is still a third of the season remaining. OU travels to face Florida at 6:45 p.m. CT Saturday at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium in Gainesville. "There ain't nothing fine," Venables said. "My challenge to them, to the players, nobody's required to be here on Monday. OK, nobody's required to be here on Monday. away.blurb: Young, who was not on the initial player availability report on Wednesday, was listed by Oklahoma State as probable going into the game on Saturday against Kansas State. Kickoff is set for noon, and the game will be broadcast on TNT. Young joined safety Quentin Hammonds, who was listed as probable on the report on Wednesday. Hammonds suffered an injury against Colorado but recovered in time to play against Iowa State. Three Cowboys remain doubtful for the game — defensive end Jaleel Johnson, linebacker Tate Romney and defensive lineman Landon Dean. Johnson and Romney both suffered injuries during the Iowa State game. Dean suffered an injury that forced him to miss games earlier this season but returned to the lineup. Wide receiver Dayvon Standard was added to the report as out, alongside tight end Carson Kolb, who is dealing with a foot injury that Morris said could keep him out another week or two. As for the Wildcats, their report remained the same as Wednesday, except for the addition of linebacker Sawyer Schilke, who is now questionable. Oklahoma State Lists Tate Romney, Jaleel Johnson as Doubtful for Kansas State Game The Oklahoma State Cowboys made a surprise adjustment to their player availability report on Thursday — wide receiver Wyatt Young. OSU, K-State Updated Injury Report Young is coming off a game in which he scored twice against the Cyclones but committed a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty after the second touchdown catch, which put the Cowboys ahead, 49-48, in the final minute of the game. The penalty forced Oklahoma State to kick off from its own 20-yard-line and helped give Iowa State better field position to maneuver for a game-winning field goal. home.blurb: Four Gators are listed as out: defensive lineman Jeramiah McCloud, tight end Evan Chieca, offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji and linebacker Jaden Robinson. "So he was not available at practice today," Jon Sumrall said on Monday . "I really don't have a really strong feeling on timeline because everything early in the week last week was trending really positively until the setback on Wednesday. It sucks. It sucks for him. He's working like hell to try to get back. He's frustrated." The two players listed as questionable are wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo. Stockton has been dealing with a nagging foot injury but still played against the Bulldogs last week, finishing with 76 yards on eight catches. Wide receiver Elijah Thomas and offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis are listed as doubtful, while wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, defensive backs Peyton Bowen and Eli Bowen, tight end Rocky Beers and defensive lineman Kenny Ozowalu are listed as questionable, and offensive lineman Jake Maikkula is listed as probable.
